IUT1.ThmA.content: Construction of Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters from initial Θ-data, with an F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry on the additive side and an F_l^*-symmetry on the multiplicative side; the Θ-link from the Θ-pilot data of one theater to the q-pilot data of another, which induces a full poly-isomorphism of the unit portions; Frobenius-pictures and étale-pictures.
explicit_hypotheses: A fixed collection of initial Θ-data (Definition 3.1).
IUT1.ThmA.conclusion: Summary statement of Corollaries 3.7 to 3.9, 4.12, 6.10, 6.12 and Definition 6.13 in introductory form.
obligations: Every term needs a definition: Frobenioids, D-prime-strips, Hodge theaters, poly-isomorphisms.
ambiguities: Introductory summary; the precise content is in the corollaries of §§3 to 6.

IUT1.ThmB.content: Let k be a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field and X a hyperbolic curve over k, with tempered fundamental group Π^tp_X and étale fundamental group Π̂_X, so that Π^tp_X ⊆ Π̂_X and Π̂_X is the profinite completion of Π^tp_X. (1) A decomposition group in Π̂_X of a closed point or cusp of X (respectively an inertia group in Π̂_X of a cusp) is contained in Π^tp_X if and only if it is a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp). (2) A Π̂_X-conjugate of Π^tp_X contains a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp) if and only if it is equal to Π^tp_X.
explicit_hypotheses: k a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field (MLF)
X a hyperbolic curve over k
Π^tp_X the tempered fundamental group and Π̂_X the étale fundamental group of X, relative to suitable basepoints, with the natural inclusion Π^tp_X ⊆ Π̂_X
IUT1.ThmB.conclusion: (1) For every decomposition group D ⊆ Π̂_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively inertia group I ⊆ Π̂_X of a cusp): D ⊆ Π^tp_X if and only if D is a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively I ⊆ Π^tp_X if and only if I is an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp). (2) For every γ ∈ Π̂_X: γ·Π^tp_X·γ^{-1} contains some decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively some inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp) if and only if γ·Π^tp_X·γ^{-1} = Π^tp_X.
external_dependencies: [SemiAnbd] tempered groups and semi-graphs of anabelioids
obligations: Tempered fundamental groups are not in Mathlib.
ambiguities: Page 16 says Theorem B is essentially Corollary 2.5 (with Remark 2.5.2), and that the stable reduction hypothesis of Corollary 2.5 is unnecessary by Proposition 2.4 (iii). This is a relation between the two statements, not part of Theorem B; Theorem B itself has no stable reduction hypothesis.

IUT1.Def1_1.content: Notation: Xu, Cu denote X, C with an underline in the paper; X→, C→ the arrow-decorated curves. Setting of page 37: l ≥ 5 an integer prime to 6; X a hyperbolic curve of type (1,1) over a field k of characteristic zero; Cu a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± over k whose k-core C also forms a k-core of X; Xu = Cu ×_C X, of type (1, l-tors); assumption (∗): G_k acts trivially on Δ_{Xu}^ab ⊗ Z/lZ. Pages 37 and 38 choose a nonzero cusp ε of Cu, use the decomposition group of the cusp 2ε to get a section σ : G_k → J_{Cu}, and obtain finite étale cyclic coverings X→ → Xu and C→ → Cu through cartesian diagrams, with Gal(C→/Cu) ≅ Z/lZ. Definition 1.1: a hyperbolic orbicurve over k isomorphic to the X→ (respectively C→) so constructed, for some choice of l and ε, is of type (1, l-tors→) (respectively (1, l-tors→)±).
explicit_hypotheses: k a field of characteristic zero
l ≥ 5 an integer prime to 6 (page 37; l is not required to be prime here)
X a hyperbolic curve of type (1,1) over k; Cu a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± over k ([EtTh] Definition 2.1) whose k-core C is also a k-core of X; Xu = Cu ×_C X
assumption (∗): the natural action of G_k on Δ_{Xu}^ab ⊗ (Z/lZ) is trivial
ε a nonzero cusp of Cu
IUT1.Def1_1.conclusion: Definition (no proof obligation): it names the types (1, l-tors→) and (1, l-tors→)± of the orbicurves X→ and C→ constructed on pages 37 and 38.
obligations: Orbicurves (stacks) are not in Mathlib.
ambiguities: The arrow decoration and the underlines were read from the rendered pages 37 to 39; Remark 1.1.1 (page 39) says the arrow denotes the archimedean ordered labels 1, 2, ... determined by the choice of ε.

IUT1.Rem1_1_1.content: The arrow decoration in X→, C→, (1, l-tors→), (1, l-tors→)± may be thought of as denoting the archimedean, ordered labels 1, 2, ..., determined by the choice of ε, on the {±1}-orbits of elements of the quotient Q in the definition of a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± ([EtTh] Definition 2.1).
IUT1.Rem1_1_1.conclusion: Notational interpretation of the arrow; no assertion.

IUT1.Rem1_1_2.content: X→ and C→ (arrow-decorated) are completely determined, up to k-isomorphism, by the data (X/k, Cu, ε) (Cu the underlined C).
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of Section 1 (pages 37 and 38) and Definition 1.1
IUT1.Rem1_1_2.conclusion: The k-isomorphism classes of X→, C→ depend only on (X/k, Cu, ε).
obligations: Stated as an observation without argument; it should follow from the construction of pages 37 and 38, which a formalization must carry out (orbicurves are not in Mathlib).

IUT1.Cor1_2.content: Notation as in IUT1.Def1_1 (Xu, Cu underlined; X→, C→ arrow-decorated). Suppose k is an NF or an MLF. There is a functorial group-theoretic algorithm that reconstructs Π_{Xu}, Π_{C→}, Π_{Cu} (respectively Π_{Cu}) together with the conjugacy classes of the decomposition groups determined by the sets of cusps {ε′, ε″}; {ε} (respectively {ε}) from Π_{X→} (respectively Π_{C→}); functoriality is with respect to isomorphisms of topological groups, and the groups are reconstructed as subgroups of Aut(Π_{X→}) (respectively Aut(Π_{C→})).
explicit_hypotheses: k an NF or an MLF
the setting of Section 1, pages 37 and 38
IUT1.Cor1_2.conclusion: Existence of a functorial group-theoretic algorithm reconstructing Π_{Xu}, Π_{C→}, Π_{Cu} (respectively Π_{Cu}) and the stated conjugacy classes of decomposition groups of cusps from Π_{X→} (respectively Π_{C→}), as subgroups of Aut(Π_{X→}) (respectively Aut(Π_{C→})).
obligations: Étale fundamental groups of orbicurves; notion of group-theoretic algorithm.
ambiguities: "Algorithm" is informal; no formal model of computation is specified.

IUT1.Rem1_2_1.content: It follows immediately from Corollary 1.2 that Aut_k(X→) = Gal(X→/Cu) (≅ Z/2lZ) and Aut_k(C→) = Gal(C→/Cu) (≅ Z/lZ), with X→, C→ arrow-decorated and Cu underlined (compare [EtTh] Remark 2.6.1).
explicit_hypotheses: k an NF or an MLF (the hypothesis of Corollary 1.2)
the setting of Section 1
IUT1.Rem1_2_1.conclusion: Aut_k(X→) = Gal(X→/Cu) ≅ Z/2lZ and Aut_k(C→) = Gal(C→/Cu) ≅ Z/lZ.
obligations: The text says it "follows immediately" from Corollary 1.2; the deduction (automorphisms of the orbicurve correspond to outer automorphisms of Π preserving the reconstructed data) must be written out.

IUT1.Rem1_2_2.content: Corrections to the group-theoretic reconstruction of decomposition groups of cusps ([AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5, based on [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9), which contains minor inaccuracies. (i) The end of the second paragraph of the proof of [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9 is replaced: given finite étale coverings Z_i → V_i → X_i with Z_i cyclic of l-power degree over V_i, total ramification of Z_i → V_i (at some point) is group-theoretic, being equivalent to a factorization Z_i → W_i → V_i with W_i → V_i of degree l and r_{W_i} < l·r_{V_i}; this extends to pro-l cyclic coverings, so by [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.7 the inertia groups of cusps in the maximal pro-l quotient (Δ_{X_i})^(l) are the maximal subgroups corresponding to coverings satisfying the condition. (ii) The end of [AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5 (iv) is replaced: the decomposition groups of cusps in H* are the maximal closed subgroups I ⊆ H* isomorphic to Z_l such that d_{χ^cyclo_G}((I^l·J)^ab ⊗ Q_l) + 1 < l·{d_{χ^cyclo_G}((I·J)^ab ⊗ Q_l) + 1} for every characteristic open subgroup J ⊆ H* with J ≠ I·J.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of [AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9 and [AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5
IUT1.Rem1_2_2.conclusion: Corrected group-theoretic characterizations of cuspidal inertia groups ([AbsAnab] Lemma 1.3.9) and of decomposition groups of cusps ([AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5 (iv)).
obligations: The equivalence of total ramification with the factorization and the inequality r_W < l·r_V is called "easily verified" (page 40); the replacement text for [AbsTopI] Lemma 4.5 (iv) is stated without proof.
Corollary 1.2 and Remark 3.1.2 (i) use this algorithm.
ambiguities: r_i, d_{χ^cyclo_G}, H* are notation of [AbsAnab] and [AbsTopI], not defined on page 40.

IUT1.Rem1_2_3.content: Related corrections to [CombGC]: (i) Galois finite étale coverings are understood to be connected. (ii) In [CombGC] Definition 1.4 (v), the cuspidal and nodal cases of purely totally ramified coverings are unnecessary, and the terminology of Definition 1.4 (vi) on descending coverings may be deleted. (iii) Replacement for [CombGC] Remark 1.4.2: for G of pro-Σ PSC-type with Σ = {l} and G' → G Galois of degree a positive power of l, a cyclic G' → G is cuspidally totally ramified if and only if r(G'') < l·r(G), with G' → G'' → G the unique factorization with G'' → G of degree l; and a Π^unr_G-covering G' → G (n(G') = deg(G'/G)·n(G)) is verticially purely totally ramified if and only if i(G') = deg(G'/G)·(i(G) − 1) + 1, equivalently i(G') − n(G') = deg(G'/G)·(i(G) − n(G) − 1) + 1. (iv) Replacement for [CombGC] Remark 1.4.3: cuspidal edge-like subgroups of Π_G are the maximal closed subgroups A ≅ Z_l such that for every characteristic open Π_{G'} ⊆ Π_G, with Π_{G''} = A·Π_{G'}, the cyclic covering G' → G'' is cuspidally totally ramified; for sturdy G, the set of vertices is characterized via the split injection ⊕_v M^unr_G[v] ↪ M^unr_G (image M^unr-vert) and elementary abelian quotients, as the set of nontrivial quotients M^unr-vert ↠ M^unr_G[v] ⊗ F_l. (v) Replacement for [CombGC] Remark 1.4.4: for noncuspidal G, the nodal edge-like subgroups are characterized similarly with nodally totally ramified coverings, equivalent to module-wise nodal ones. (vi), (vii) Replacement texts for the second and final paragraphs of the proof of [CombGC] Theorem 1.6, deriving group-theoretic cuspidality and assertion (iii) from Remarks 1.4.3 and 1.4.2.
explicit_hypotheses: G a semi-graph of anabelioids of pro-Σ PSC-type with Σ = {l} (as in [CombGC])
IUT1.Rem1_2_3.conclusion: Corrected characterizations of cuspidally and verticially purely totally ramified coverings, of cuspidal and nodal edge-like subgroups and of the set of vertices, and corrected proof steps of [CombGC] Theorem 1.6.
definitions_required: semi-graph of anabelioids of PSC-type [CombGC] Definition 1.1
obligations: Each characterization is introduced with "one verifies immediately"; only the sufficiency in (iv) has a short argument (finiteness of the set of cusps gives a compatible system of cusps stabilized by A).
ambiguities: The symbols r, i, n (underlined in the paper) are the invariants of [CombGC] Remark 1.1.3; they are not defined on these pages.
Page 42 writes the vertex characterization for sturdy G only.

Λ ⊆ Π^tp_G a nontrivial compact subgroup

IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.connected_anabelioid.content: Definition: a category is a connected anabelioid if it is equivalent to B(G) for some profinite group G (with fixed universe levels). Theorems: B(G) is a connected anabelioid; every Galois category in the sense of Mathlib is a connected anabelioid (via Mathlib's equivalence with finite continuous Aut F-sets of a fiber functor F). Definitions: a bundled connected anabelioid; the full subcategory of objects connected in the sense of Mathlib's Galois categories.
IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.connected_anabelioid.covers: The Geometry of Anabelioids page 9: Definition 1.1.1 and one direction of Remark 1.1.1.1 (a Galois category is a connected anabelioid).
IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.connected_anabelioid.not_covered: The converse of Remark 1.1.1.1 (a connected anabelioid is a Galois category; Mathlib has no transport of GaloisCategory along an equivalence); agreement of Mathlib's connected objects with the definition on Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 7; anabelioids that are not connected; Example 1.1.3.
ambiguities: Universes: the paper fixes one Grothendieck universe; here B(G) for G in universe u uses finite types in universe w and the predicate fixes both levels.

Connected objects use Mathlib's PreGaloisCategory.IsConnected (not initial, no proper non-initial subobject), not the wording of Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 7 (not a coproduct of two nonempty objects).

IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.semi_graph_of_anabelio.content: Definition: a semi-graph of anabelioids over a semi-graph assigns a connected anabelioid to each vertex and each edge and, to each branch b of an edge e abutting to a vertex v, a morphism of anabelioids from the anabelioid of e to that of v, that is, an exact functor from the anabelioid of v to that of e. Example: on any semi-graph, the constant semi-graph of anabelioids with every constituent B(G) and identity branch functors.
IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.semi_graph_of_anabelio.conclusion: A definition and a nonvacuity example.
IUT1.Prop2_1.frag.semi_graph_of_anabelio.covers: Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 22, Definition 2.1 (a) to (c): the object G of the discussion preceding Proposition 2.1 of IUT I (page 44), without the PSC-type condition.

IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph.content: Definition: a semi-graph is a type of vertices, a type of edges, a type of branches with a map to edges whose every fiber has exactly two elements, and a coincidence map sending each branch to the vertex it abuts to or to none. Further definitions: an edge abuts to a vertex; verticial cardinality; graphs; finite and countable semi-graphs; components; an edge joins two vertices; closed, open and isolated edges; coverticial edges; locally finite and untangled semi-graphs; the incidence graph and connectedness through it; joints. Lemmas: the branches of an edge form a finite type; verticial cardinality is at most two; in a graph every edge abuts to a vertex.
IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph.conclusion: Definitions with elementary lemmas, all proved.
IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph.covers: Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 11 (definition of a semi-graph, verticial portion and cardinality, graphs, branches, finite and countable, components, joins, abuts to), pages 12 and 13 (closed, open, isolated and coverticial edges; locally finite, untangled, joint). The semi-graph underlying the semi-graph of anabelioids of IUT I page 44.
IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph.not_covered: The topological space of a semi-graph and the proof that connectedness of the incidence graph is its connectedness; trees; subjoints. Of Proposition 2.2: PSC-type, fundamental groups, decomposition subgroups, commensurable terminality.
ambiguities: An edge of the page is a set of exactly two branches (not at most two); here the branches form one type with a map to edges whose fibers have exactly two elements, a reencoding of the same data.

The page defines connectedness through the associated topological space, which is not constructed; connectedness is taken as connectedness (with nonemptiness) of the incidence graph of vertices and edges.
The same declarations also serve IUT1.Prop2_1 (and, through the notation of IUT I Section 2, Corollary 2.5 and Theorem B, whose pages were not read for these records).

IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph_morphism.content: Definition: a morphism of semi-graphs consists of maps on vertices, edges and branches, a branch of e going to a branch of the image of e, injective on the branches of each edge, and compatible with the coincidence maps on branches that abut to a vertex; identity and composition; proper morphisms (preserving verticial cardinality), immersions and excisions (injective, respectively bijective, on branches abutting to each vertex), graph-coverings (proper excisions). Lemmas: a morphism is bijective on the branches of each edge; a morphism does not decrease verticial cardinality.
IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph_morphism.conclusion: Definitions with two lemmas, all proved.
IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph_morphism.covers: Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 11 (the paragraph defining morphisms, including its last sentence on verticial cardinality) and pages 13 and 14 (immersions, excisions, proper morphisms, graph-coverings).

IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.sub_semi_graph.content: Definition: the sub-semi-graph of a semi-graph with given sets of vertices and edges, whose branches are those lying on the chosen edges and whose coincidence map keeps a vertex when it is chosen and gives none otherwise; its inclusion morphism; the maximal subgraph (all vertices, closed edges only). Lemmas: conditions (b) and (c) of page 12 hold; keeping all vertices does not change verticial cardinality; the maximal subgraph is a graph.
IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.sub_semi_graph.covers: Semi-graphs of Anabelioids page 12 (definition of a sub-semi-graph, conditions (a) to (c)) and page 13 (maximal subgraph). These are the connected sub-semi-graph H and the maximal subgraph named on IUT I page 44.

IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.compactification.content: Definition: the compactification of a semi-graph, adding one new vertex for each branch abutting to no vertex, to which that branch then abuts; the morphism from a semi-graph to its compactification. Lemmas: in the compactification every branch abuts to a vertex; the compactification is a graph; a branch abuts to an old vertex v in the compactification exactly when it abuts to v in the original semi-graph.

IUT1.Prop2_2.frag.semi_graph_examples.content: Examples: a vertex with an open edge (the edge is open and not isolated, the semi-graph is not a graph, is untangled and connected); a loop (a connected graph with a closed edge, not untangled); two vertices joined by a closed edge (a connected, untangled, locally finite graph whose edge joins the two vertices); a joint (one vertex, two open edges). IUT1.Cor2_3.content: Setting (pages 46, 47): k an MLF with residue characteristic p, X a hyperbolic curve over k with stable reduction over O_k; Π^tp_X, Δ^tp_X the Σ̂-tempered quotients of the tempered fundamental groups; Δ̂_X the pro-Σ̂ fundamental group of X_k̄, Π̂_X the corresponding quotient; inclusions Π^tp_X ↪ Π̂_X, Δ^tp_X ↪ Δ̂_X. Assume p ∉ Σ, G is the pro-Σ semi-graph of anabelioids of the special fiber of the stable model 𝒳, and the sub-semi-graph H ⊆ G is stabilized by G_k; so Δ^tp_X ↠ Π^tp_G and Δ̂_X ↠ Π̂_G. Then: (i) Δ^tp_{X,H} = Δ^tp_X ×_{Π^tp_G} Π^tp_H ⊆ Δ^tp_X and Δ̂_{X,H} = Δ̂_X ×_{Π̂_G} Π̂_H ⊆ Δ̂_X are commensurably terminal, so the outer G_k-actions on Δ^tp_X, Δ̂_X induce outer actions on Δ^tp_{X,H}, Δ̂_{X,H}. (ii) The closure of Δ^tp_{X,H} in Δ̂_X is Δ̂_{X,H}. (iii) If (a) Σ̂ contains a prime l ∉ Σ ∪ {p}, or (b) Σ̂ = Primes, then Δ̂_{X,H} is slim, and there are exact sequences of center-free groups 1 → Δ^tp_{X,H} → Π^tp_{X,H} → G_k → 1 and 1 → Δ̂_{X,H} → Π̂_{X,H} → G_k → 1, with Π^tp_{X,H}, Π̂_{X,H} defined so as to make them exact. (iv) Under (iii)'s hypothesis, the images of Π^tp_{X,H} ↪ Π^tp_X and Π̂_{X,H} ↪ Π̂_X are commensurably terminal. (v) Δ̂_{X,H} ∩ Δ^tp_X = Δ^tp_{X,H} in Δ̂_X. (vi) For an inertia group I_x ⊆ Δ^tp_X (respectively Δ̂_X) of a cusp x of X, with ξ the cusp of 𝒳 corresponding to x: I_x lies in a Δ^tp_X- (respectively Δ̂_X-) conjugate of Δ^tp_{X,H} (respectively Δ̂_{X,H}) if and only if ξ meets an irreducible component of the special fiber contained in H.

IUT1.Rem2_5_3.content: Corrections to [SemiAnbd]. (i) Terminology: (T1) a tempered group is Galois-countable if its topology has a countable basis, extended to (quasi-)temperoids; (T2) a semi-graph of anabelioids G is Galois-countable if countable with a countable collection of finite étale coverings G_i → G such that every finite étale covering becomes split over some G_i componentwise; (T3) G is strictly coherent if coherent ([SemiAnbd] Definition 2.3 (iii)) with component groups generated by N elements for a fixed N (finite coherent implies strictly coherent). (T4) Strictly coherent countable semi-graphs are Galois-countable. (T5), (T6) Under Galois-countability, the tempered fundamental groups of [SemiAnbd] Remark 3.2.1 and before Proposition 3.6 are well defined and Galois-countable; countability makes the nonabelian R^1 lim obstruction to compatible basepoints vanish. (ii) Effects (E1) to (E9): subquotients of absolute Galois groups of countable fields, and tame arithmetic fundamental groups over such fields ([AbsTopI] Proposition 2.2), are Galois-countable; no effect on [SemiAnbd] Examples 2.10, 3.10, 5.6, §§1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and the Appendix; Galois-countability must be assumed in [SemiAnbd] 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, 3.8, 3.9 and throughout [QuCnf], [FrdII]; no effect elsewhere. (iii) The assertion in the second display of [SemiAnbd] Remark 2.4.2 is false as stated (Dehn twists of [SemiAnbd] Example 2.10 give a counterexample); it is replaced by: the isomorphism classes of the φ_v determine those of each φ_e and each φ_b up to composition with an automorphism of G_e → H_f → H_w arising from an automorphism of G_e → H_f; the subsequent discussion also needs every edge to abut to at least one vertex. (iv) In the proof of [SemiAnbd] Proposition 3.2, "is Galois" should read "is a countable coproduct of Galois objects". (v) Two wording corrections to [SemiAnbd] Definition 3.5 (ii). (vi) In [SemiAnbd] Definition 5.1 (i), conditions (c), (d) are strengthened to (c^new) (trivial action of H on G and continuity of H → Aut(G[c]) for the profinite topology from (O1), (O2)) and (d^new) (a finite set C* of components with compatible isomorphisms G[c] ⥲ G[c*]); by [NS] Theorem 1.1 (c) and (c^new) hold automatically since H is topologically finitely generated; the strengthening has no effect on the rest of [SemiAnbd].
IUT1.Rem2_5_3.conclusion: Corrections to [SemiAnbd] and [QuCnf], [FrdII]: Galois-countability hypotheses must be added in the listed places; one assertion of [SemiAnbd] Remark 2.4.2 is false and is replaced; Definition 5.1 (i) is strengthened. The text asserts that none of this affects IUT I.

IUT1.Thm2_6.content: Let F be a group containing a finite index subgroup G that is a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable topological surface of genus ≥ 2, and H ⊆ F an infinite subgroup. Regard H, G ⊆ F ⊆ F̂ (F is residually finite), F̂ the profinite completion. Let γ ∈ F̂ with γ·H·γ^{-1} ⊆ F. Write H_G = H ∩ G. Then γ ∈ F·N_F̂(H_G), that is, γ·H_G·γ^{-1} = δ·H_G·δ^{-1} for some δ ∈ F. If moreover H_G is nonabelian, then γ ∈ F.

IUT1.Lem2_7.content: Let G be as in Theorem 2.6 (free of finite rank, or an orientable surface group of genus ≥ 2) and Ĝ its profinite completion. (i) Any subgroup of G generated by two elements is free. (ii) For x ∈ G, x ≠ 1, there is a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G with x ∈ G_1 and x of nontrivial image in G_1^ab. (iii) For noncommuting x, y ∈ G there are a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G and n ≥ 1 with x^n, y^n ∈ G_1 whose images in G_1^ab generate a free abelian subgroup of rank two. (iv) Every abelian subgroup of G is cyclic. (v) If T̂ ⊆ Ĝ is a closed subgroup and there is a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing an isomorphism T̂ ≅ Ẑ, then T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ. (vi) If G is nonabelian and N̂ = Ker(Ĝ ↠ Ĝ^ab), the centralizer Z_Ĝ(N̂) is trivial. (vii) In the notation of (vi), an automorphism of the profinite group Ĝ that preserves N̂ and restricts to the identity on N̂ is the identity.

Ĝ the profinite completion of G
(ii): x ∈ G, x ≠ 1

(v): T̂ ⊆ Ĝ closed, with a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing T̂ ≅ Ẑ
(vi), (vii): G nonabelian; (vii): α an automorphism of Ĝ preserving N̂ with α|_N̂ = id
IUT1.Lem2_7.conclusion: (i) two-generated subgroups are free; (ii) separation of x ≠ 1 in the abelianization of a finite index subgroup; (iii) x^n, y^n span a rank two free abelian subgroup of G_1^ab; (iv) abelian subgroups are cyclic; (v) T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ; (vi) Z_Ĝ(N̂) = {1}; (vii) α = id.

IUT1.Rem3_1_2.content: (i) The open subgroup Π_{X_K} ⊆ Π_{C_K} (arrow-decorated X_K, C_K) can be constructed group-theoretically from the topological group Π_{C_K}. (ii) Convention, the Θ-approach: the reconstruction algorithm of [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 is applied not to Π_{C_K} but to the open subgroup Π_{X_K}, reconstructing the function field of X_K with its natural action of Gal(X_K/C_K) ≅ Π_{C_K}/Π_{X_K}; similarly at v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non (respectively V^bad) to Π_{C_v} or, via Corollary 1.2, Π_{X_v}, Π_{C_v} with arrow decorations (respectively to Π^tp_{C_v} or, via [EtTh] Proposition 2.4, Π^tp of the double-underlined X_v). All uses of [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 and its consequences in the series are via the Θ-approach. (iii) From the tautological extension 1 → Δ_Θ → Δ^Θ_X → Δ^ell_X → 1 of [EtTh] §2, with Δ_Θ = [Δ_X, Δ_X]/[Δ_X, [Δ_X, Δ_X]], Δ^Θ_X = Δ_X/[Δ_X, [Δ_X, Δ_X]], Δ^ell_X = Δ^ab_X, its class in H^2(Δ^ell_X, Δ_Θ) gives a tautological isomorphism M_X ⥲ Δ_Θ (M_X ≅ Hom(H^2(Δ^ell_X, Ẑ), Ẑ) by [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 (b)), and hence M_{Xu} ⥲ (l·Δ_Θ) since [Δ_X : Δ_{Xu}] = l (Xu the underlined X). This isomorphism is a characteristic subquotient of Π_{C_{F_mod}}, with a natural conjugation action; the significance of the Θ-approach lies in this isomorphism, used in [IUTchII] at bad v, relating the cyclotome M_X to (l·Δ_Θ), central in the cyclotomic rigidity of [EtTh] Corollary 2.19 (i). (iv) For large l, the role of the covering X in the Θ-approach recalls that of the universal covering of a complex elliptic curve by C in [AbsTopIII] §2.

IUT1.Rem3_1_5.content: Since the 3-torsion points of E_F are rational over F and F is Galois over F_mod (Definition 3.1 (b)), K is Galois over F_mod (citing [IUTchIV] Proposition 1.8 (iv)). Define the algebraic stack S_mod = Spec(O_K)//Gal(K/F_mod) (stack-theoretic quotient). A finite extension L ⊆ F̄ of F_mod gives, by integral closure of S_mod in L, a stack S_{mod,L}; arithmetic line bundles on such stacks give, for any finite quotient Gal(F̄/F_mod) ↠ Q, a Frobenioid by the easily verified stack-theoretic version of [FrdI] Example 6.3, for which an analogue of [FrdI] Theorem 6.4 holds. After passing to the perfection or the realification these become naturally isomorphic to the non-stack-theoretic versions.

(b), (c): "one verifies immediately" that the analogue of [FrdI] Theorem 6.4 holds; no argument is given.

IUT1.Rem3_1_7.content: Special rational functions on the model of C_F. (i) The model C_{F_mod} and κ-coric rational functions. (ii) ∞κ-coric and ∞κ×-coric functions and their pseudo-monoids. (iii) κ-solvable functions, the subgroup Gal(K/F(μ_l)) and a linear disjointness. (iv) κ-sol-automorphisms and the center-freeness of Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)).
explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data as in Definition 3.1
IUT1.Rem3_1_7.conclusion: (i) C_{F_mod} exists uniquely and κ-coric functions are defined, with their elementary consequences. (ii) A κ-coric function of degree 4 exists; every element of L (respectively L^□) is a value of a κ-coric function at a non-critical point; ∞κ- and ∞κ×-coric functions form divisible cyclotomic pseudo-monoids. (iii) L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) are linearly disjoint over F(μ_l)·L_C. (iv) Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) is center-free, so the conjugation square to Aut^{κ-sol}, Out^{κ-sol} is cartesian.
obligations: See the child records.

IUT1.Rem3_1_7.i.content: By the definition of F_mod and K-coricity of C_K, C_F has a model C_{F_mod} over F_mod, unique up to unique isomorphism; C_v is its base change to (F_mod)_v. Let L be F_mod or (F_mod)_v, C_L the model over L, L̄_C an algebraic closure of the function field L_C, L̄ the induced algebraic closure of L. The coarse space |C_L| is isomorphic to the affine line over L. A closed point of a proper smooth curve given by a finite subextension of L̄_C is critical if it maps to a point of |C_L|^cpt arising from a 2-torsion point of E_F, and strictly critical if moreover it does not map to the point arising from the unique cusp of C_L. A rational function f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if: whenever f ∉ L, over L̄ f has precisely one pole and at least two distinct zeroes; its divisor of zeroes and poles is defined over a number field and avoids the critical points; f restricts to a root of unity at every strictly critical point of |C_L|^cpt.
explicit_hypotheses: initial Θ-data as in Definition 3.1
L = F_mod or L = (F_mod)_v for some v ∈ V_mod
IUT1.Rem3_1_7.i.conclusion: Existence and uniqueness of the model C_{F_mod}; |C_L| ≅ A^1_L; definition of critical and strictly critical points and of κ-coric functions. Consequences stated: for f ∉ L, f and f^{-1} are never both κ-coric; if c ∈ L and both f and c·f are κ-coric, then c is a root of unity; restriction to strictly critical points gives a splitting, up to roots of unity, of nonzero constant multiples of κ-coric functions into κ-coric functions times L^×.
obligations: Uniqueness of the model and |C_L| ≅ A^1_L are said to follow immediately ("one verifies immediately") from the definitions.
The consequences about f^{-1} and c·f are direct from the definition (one pole; values at strictly critical points) and could be checked once the objects are defined.
ambiguities: Critical points are defined on proper smooth curves of finite subextensions of L̄_C, but the root-of-unity condition is stated on |C_L|^cpt itself (page 67).

IUT1.Rem3_1_7.ii.content: Let L^□ be an intermediate field between L and L̄ that is solvably closed ([GlSol] Definition 1 (i)). Since |C_L|^cpt has precisely 4 critical points, there is a κ-coric f_sol ∈ L_C of degree 4. Hence every element of L (respectively L^□) is a value of some κ-coric function on C_L at some non-critical L- (respectively L^□-) valued point (elementary theory of polynomials on the affine line with Hensel's lemma, as in the proof of [AbsTopII] Lemma 2.1; respectively f_sol and solvability of S_4). With U_L̄ = L̄^× if L = F_mod and the units of L̄ if L = (F_mod)_v: f ∈ L̄_C is ∞κ-coric if some power f^n is a κ-coric element of L_C, and ∞κ×-coric if c·f is ∞κ-coric for some c ∈ U_L̄; f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if and only if it is ∞κ-coric. An ∞κ×-coric f is ∞κ-coric if and only if it restricts to a root of unity at some (equivalently every) strictly critical point. Multiplication gives pseudo-monoid structures on κ-, ∞κ-, ∞κ×-coric functions; the latter two are divisible and cyclotomic.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Rem3_1_7.i
L^□ a solvably closed intermediate field between L and L̄
IUT1.Rem3_1_7.ii.conclusion: Existence of a degree-4 κ-coric f_sol; every element of L, respectively L^□, is a value of a κ-coric function at a non-critical point; definitions of ∞κ- and ∞κ×-coric functions; the characterization of ∞κ-coric among ∞κ×-coric functions; the pseudo-monoid structures.
obligations: Each claim is said to "follow immediately" or to be verified immediately; the existence of f_sol and the value statements need the elementary theory of polynomials on the affine line, Hensel's lemma, and solvability of S_4 (in Mathlib).
The claim that |C_L|^cpt has precisely 4 critical points rests on E_F having four 2-torsion points mapping to distinct points of the coarse space.
ambiguities: Page 67 says f ∈ L_C is κ-coric if and only if it is ∞κ-coric, although the definition of ∞κ-coric is for f ∈ L̄_C; the statement is read as concerning f ∈ L_C.

IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iii.content: Assume L = F_mod, L̄ = F̄. f ∈ L̄_C is κ-solvable if it is an F^×_sol-multiple of a ∞κ-coric element of L̄_C; equivalently some power f^n is a ∞κ×-coric element of F_sol·L_C. Let F(μ_l) ⊆ K be generated by the l-th roots of unity, L_C(κ-sol) ⊆ L̄_C generated by κ-solvable elements, L_C(C_K) ⊆ L̄_C generated over L_C by the images of the F(μ_l)·L_C-linear embeddings of the function field of C_K. Since F/F_mod is Galois of degree prime to l (Definition 3.1 (b)), Gal(K/F(μ_l)) ⊆ Gal(K/F_mod) is normal and is the unique subgroup abstractly isomorphic to SL_2(F_l) (Remark 3.1.5; [GenEll] Lemma 3.1 (i)). Since SL_2(F_l) is perfect ([GenEll] Lemma 3.1 (ii)), and by the definition of ∞κ×-coric (zeroes and poles avoid critical points), L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) are linearly disjoint over F(μ_l)·L_C inside L̄_C. Hence Gal(L_C(C_K)/F(μ_l)·L_C) ⥲ Gal(L_C(C_K)·L_C(κ-sol)/F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol)) naturally.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Rem3_1_7.ii
L = F_mod and L̄ = F̄
IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iii.conclusion: Characterization of κ-solvable elements; Gal(K/F(μ_l)) is normal in Gal(K/F_mod) and the unique subgroup isomorphic to SL_2(F_l); linear disjointness of L_C(C_K) and F(μ_l)·L_C(κ-sol) over F(μ_l)·L_C; the natural isomorphism of Galois groups.
obligations: The linear disjointness is said to "follow immediately" from perfectness of SL_2(F_l) and the definition of ∞κ×-coric; the argument (an abelian or solvable quotient of a perfect group is trivial) must be written out, including why L_C(κ-sol) is a solvable extension.
The SL_2(F_l) characterization rests on [GenEll] Lemma 3.1 and on Definition 3.1 (b), (c).

IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iv.content: With the exact sequence 1 → Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) → Gal(L̄_C/L_C) → Gal(L_C(κ-sol)/L_C) → 1, call a subgroup of Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) κ-sol-open if it is the intersection with it of a normal open subgroup of Gal(L̄_C/L_C). The groups Aut^{κ-sol} ⊆ Aut and Out^{κ-sol} ⊆ Out of (outer) automorphisms of Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) preserving each κ-sol-open subgroup admit compatible homomorphisms to Aut(Q), Out(Q) for each quotient by a κ-sol-open subgroup; their kernels define profinite topologies, for which the conjugation diagram Gal(L̄_C/L_C) → Aut^{κ-sol}, Gal(L_C(κ-sol)/L_C) → Out^{κ-sol} is a commutative diagram of continuous homomorphisms. Moreover Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) is center-free, so the diagram is cartesian.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iii
IUT1.Rem3_1_7.iv.conclusion: Gal(L̄_C/L_C(κ-sol)) is center-free; hence the commutative square formed by Gal(L̄_C/L_C), Aut^{κ-sol}, Gal(L_C(κ-sol)/L_C), Out^{κ-sol} is cartesian.
obligations: Proof sketch (page 69): Gal(F̄·L_C(κ-sol)/F̄·L_C) is abelian; by Lemma 2.7 (vi), (vii) applied to the geometric fundamental groups of genus zero affine hyperbolic curves with function field L_C, a central element α acts trivially on such a (center-free) geometric fundamental group; by the Galois injectivity of [NodNon] Theorem C (a case known to Belyi), α is the identity.
That center-freeness implies the square is cartesian is elementary group theory and could be checked separately.

IUT1.Rem3_2_4.content: Corrections to the tempered Frobenioids of [EtTh] §§3, 4. Let ℨ^log_∞ be the universal combinatorial covering of the formal log scheme of a stable log curve with split special fiber over the integers of a finite extension of an MLF of residue characteristic p, with generic fiber Z^log. (i) For a nonzero meromorphic function f on ℨ^log_∞ consider: (a) for every N ≥ 1, f has an N-th root over some tempered covering of Z^log; (b) the same for N prime to p; (c) the divisor of zeroes and poles of f is a log-divisor. Then (a) ⇒ (b) is immediate, (b) ⇒ (c) by ramification divisors, and (c) ⇒ (b) via admissible coverings ([PrfGC] §2, §8): a finite log étale covering Y^log → Z^log whose pull-back annihilates ramification over cusps and special fiber (R1) and splits extensions of function fields of irreducible components (R2), so that f has an N-th root over the universal combinatorial covering of Y^log. Hence (a) ⇒ (b) ⇔ (c); whether (c) implies (a) is stated to be unclear to the author. (ii) The theta function of [EtTh] satisfies (a) ([EtTh] §1, Proposition 1.3). (iii) [EtTh] Definition 3.1 (ii) defines log-meromorphic by (c), but the proof of [EtTh] Proposition 4.2 (iii) needs (a). (iv) Remedies: (A) redefine log-meromorphic by (a) (perhaps "tempered-meromorphic"), or (B) require in [EtTh] Definition 4.1 (i) the category-theoretic condition (d): for every N ≥ 1 there is a linear morphism A' → A in C with the pull-back of f admitting an N-th root. (v) (A) changes the definition of tempered Frobenioid slightly; (B) only reduces the range of applicability of [EtTh] §4 (irrelevant for the theta functions); the series adopts (A). (vi) Three textual modifications to [EtTh] Example 3.9 (i), (ii) concerning Φ^ell_W: Y^log of genus 1 with precisely one cusp or two cusps differing by 2-torsion; the lower arrow written Ẋ^log → Ċ^log; unramified over the cusps and the generic points of the special fibers, with tempered admissible coverings.

IUT1.Rem3_4_2.content: The Kummer structure κ_v : O^▷(C_v) ↪ A_{D_v} of Example 3.4 (i) may be viewed as follows. In the terminology of [AbsTopIII] Definition 2.1 (i), (iv), the CAF structure on Ā_{D_v} determines, by pull-back via κ_v, an Aut-holomorphic structure on the groupification O^▷(C_v)^gp together with a tautological co-holomorphicization O^▷(C_v)^gp → A_{D_v}. Conversely, from this Aut-holomorphic structure and co-holomorphicization one recovers the inclusion of topological monoids κ_v (by [AbsTopIII] Corollary 2.3 and the fact that every holomorphic automorphism of C^× preserving the elements of norm ≤ 1 is the identity). Thus κ_v is equivalent to the pair (Aut-holomorphic structure, co-holomorphicization). The co-holomorphicization, unlike the inclusion of monoids, is compatible with the logarithm of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 4.5.

IUT1.Rem3_4_2.conclusion: The Kummer structure κ_v is equivalent to the Aut-holomorphic structure on O^▷(C_v)^gp together with the co-holomorphicization O^▷(C_v)^gp → A_{D_v}; the co-holomorphicization is compatible with the logarithm of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 4.5.

By the holomorphic elliptic cuspidalization of [AbsTopIII] Corollary 2.7 there is a natural isomorphism of CAF's Ā_{X_v} = Ā_{D_v} ⥲ Ā_{E_v} (X_v arrow-decorated), natural from the viewpoint of the Θ-approach. (ii) Belyi cuspidalization ([AbsTopII] Example 3.6, Corollaries 3.7, 3.8; [AbsTopIII] Remark 2.8.3) admits a holomorphic analogue, holomorphic Belyi cuspidalization, with details left to the reader; consequently the set of NF-points of the underlying topological space of D_v can be reconstructed by a functorial algorithm from the abstract Aut-holomorphic space D_v.

IUT1.Rem3_9_3.content: (i) The mono-analytic core {D^⊢_v}_{v∈V} may be thought of as a fixed underlying real-analytic surface on which holomorphic structures are imposed, and the Frobenius-picture as a global arithmetic analogue of a Teichmüller geodesic, or of the canonical liftings of p-adic Teichmüller theory. (ii) Along a Teichmüller geodesic one real dimension is dilated and one fixed; in the Frobenius-picture of Corollary 3.8 the local units O^× correspond to the fixed dimension and the local value groups undergo Θ-dilations; treating them independently uses the characteristic splittings of the split Frobenioids of Examples 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, which at bad v correspond to the constant multiple rigidity of the étale theta function. (iii) In complex Teichmüller theory the two real dimensions are the real and imaginary parts of the coordinate obtained by locally integrating the square root of a square differential, whose only indeterminacy, multiplication by −1, preserves real and imaginary parts; for n ≥ 3, integrating n-th roots of sections of the n-th tensor power of differentials gives an indeterminacy by n-th roots of unity that confuses real and imaginary parts. (iv) Linear movement along the oriented graph Γ of Corollary 3.8 corresponds to the linear flow along a Teichmüller geodesic, and the rotation of ⊞ and ⊠ of [IUTchIII] to rotations about a fixed point, or in the p-adic analogy to Frobenius in positive characteristic.
IUT1.Rem3_9_3.conclusion: Heuristic analogy between the Frobenius-picture and Teichmüller geodesics; the only mathematical observation is the classical one in (iii) that multiplication by −1 preserves real and imaginary parts while multiplication by an n-th root of unity, n ≥ 3, does not.
ambiguities: Heuristic remark; no claim to formalize beyond the elementary observation in (iii).

IUT1.Rem4_3_1.content: (i) Assume F = F_mod. Spec(K) → Spec(F) has no section; this is related to the nonexistence of a global multiplicative subspace ([HASurII] Remark 3.7), viewed as the principal obstruction to applying the scheme-theoretic Hodge-Arakelov theory of [HASurI], [HASurII] to diophantine geometry. Via the arrows φ^NF_j of Example 4.3 (iv), the D-prime-strips may be seen as arithmetic collections of local analytic (local-analytic) sections of Spec(K) → Spec(F) (Fig. 4.1), each yielding an arithmetic local-analytic global multiplicative subspace and global canonical generator. (ii) Their failure to be globally arithmetically holomorphic is seen from three related viewpoints: (a) they do not extend to ring homomorphisms K → F; (b) an identification of a prime v of F with a prime v' of K does not extend to an isomorphism of prime decomposition trees ([NSW] Theorem 12.2.5), compared with [IUTchIV] §3 and the membership relation; (c) the isomorphisms of local absolute Galois groups do not extend to a section G_F ↠ G_K of the inclusion G_K ↪ G_F. By the Neukirch-Uchida theorem (a) and (c) are essentially equivalent, and (b) is closely related. (iii) Understanding this failure is a central theme of the series.
explicit_hypotheses: F = F_mod (assumed for simplicity, page 101)
IUT1.Rem4_3_1.conclusion: Interpretive remark; the mathematical assertions are that Spec(K) → Spec(F) has no section (K ≠ F) and the facts (a), (b), (c) with the essential equivalence of (a) and (c) via Neukirch-Uchida.
ambiguities: "Essentially equivalent" and "closely related" (page 102) are not made precise.

IUT1.Rem4_3_2.content: The incompatibility of the arithmetic local-analytic sections with global prime distributions and global Galois groups is the technical obstacle that requires, in [IUTchIII], the absolute p-adic mono-anabelian geometry of [AbsTopIII] (panalocalization along prime-strips). The desired geometry must satisfy: (a) local independence of global structures; (b) globalizability independent of local structures (Fig. 4.3); (c) being based on étale-like structures, so as to give canonical splittings as in the étale-picture of Corollary 3.9 (i). (a) and (b) almost appear to contradict each other; for function fields of dimension one their simultaneous realization seems to require descending to the base field. It is said to be a highly nontrivial consequence of [AbsTopIII] that its mono-anabelian geometry satisfies (a), (b), (c).
IUT1.Rem4_3_2.conclusion: Methodological requirements (a), (b), (c) and the assertion that the mono-anabelian geometry of [AbsTopIII] satisfies them.
obligations: Properties (a), (b), (c) are informal; to check the assertion about [AbsTopIII] they must first be made precise.
ambiguities: Properties (a), (b), (c) are stated informally (page 103); no precise formulation is given.

IUT1.Rem4_3_3.content: Analogy between the mono-anabelian theory of [AbsTopIII] and the classical geometry of the upper half-plane H. (i) Composing the analogy with Frobenius-invariant indigenous bundles in p-adic Teichmüller theory and the p-adic/complex analogy of [pOrd], [pTeich] gives an analogy with H, whose canonical Kähler (Poincaré) metric relates the theory to classical Arakelov theory. (ii) The diagram (∗) Π ↷ k̄^× → (log) k̄ ↶ Π (k a finite extension of Q_p, Π the arithmetic fundamental group of a hyperbolic orbicurve over k, log the p-adic logarithm) is compared with the tautological indigenous bundle (E, ∇_E) on H: Hodge filtration 0 → ω → E → τ → 0 with τ = ω^{-1}, complex conjugation ι_E, the Hermitian metric |−|_ω from ω ↪ E → E ↠ τ, and κ_H = (1/2πi) ∂∂̄ log(|f|²_ω) for a trivializing section f, the canonical Kähler metric. The log in κ_H recalls the log-Frobenius operation; Π recalls ∂; ∂̄ recalls Π on the opposite side of log; the Hodge filtration corresponds to the ring structures on either side of log; log-shells as canonical units of volume correspond to κ_H determining volume on H. (iii) Properties (a), (b) of Remark 4.3.2 correspond to local representability of global degree via κ_H on a compact quotient S of H, and to the canonical global extension of κ_H over S. (iv) A table summarizes the analogy.
IUT1.Rem4_3_3.conclusion: Heuristic analogy; the only formula is the standard definition κ_H = (1/2πi) ∂∂̄ log(|f|²_ω) of the Kähler form from the Hermitian metric on ω.
ambiguities: The remark states analogies, not theorems; no claim requires proof.

IUT1.Rem4_5_1.content: (i) For a group G and subgroups J ⊆ H ⊆ G known only up to G-conjugacy (independent G-conjugacy indeterminacies), with H^g = g·H·g^{-1}: the inclusion ι : J ↪ H cannot be distinguished from its conjugates, and possibly J^g ⊆ H for some g with (H, J) and (H, J^g) not isomorphic as pairs. The collection of factorizations J ↪ H ↪ G (outer homomorphisms compatible with the structure morphisms), namely the inclusions J^{g1} ↪ H^{g2}, is well defined compatibly with the indeterminacies, while specifying ι independently of ζ : J ↪ H^{g^{-1}} imposes a partial synchronization (deactivation) at the cost of arbitrary choices. (ii) For a G-conjugate H* of H and I ⊆ H*, the condition (∗⊆) that I be a G-conjugate of J is independent of H*, while (∗≅) that additionally (H*, I) ≅ (H, J) depends on H*; similarly (∗⊇) for I ⊇ J*. (iii) At v ∈ V^bad in Example 4.5 (i), G = π1(D^⊚), H = the image of π1(D_{v_j}), J = the index l subgroup of a cuspidal inertia group; the indeterminacies cannot be naturally synchronized (such a synchronization would amount to a Galois-equivariant splitting of prime decomposition trees, which is absurd), yet by Corollary 2.5 the factorization J ↪ H ↪ G is uniquely determined by the G-conjugate of J. (iv) At v ∈ V^arc the factorization is not uniquely determined (Remark 2.6.1), but by Corollary 2.8 the H-conjugacy class of the image of J is. (v) Only the bad-v case matters for the series, in the Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of [IUTchII].

(iii), (iv): the setting of Example 4.5 (i) at v ∈ V^bad, respectively v ∈ V^arc

(iii): at bad v the factorization is uniquely determined by the composite J ↪ G (Corollary 2.5). (iv): at archimedean v only the H-conjugacy class of the image of J is determined (Corollary 2.8).

IUT1.Def4_6.content: (i) D-NF-bridge: a poly-morphism D_J → D^⊚ from a capsule of D-prime-strips, isomorphic to the model by conjugation; morphisms are pairs (capsule-full poly-isomorphism, Aut_ε-orbit of isomorphisms) compatible with the arrows. (ii) D-Θ-bridge: a poly-morphism D_J → D_>, isomorphic to the model; morphisms are pairs (capsule-full poly-isomorphism, full poly-isomorphism). (iii) D-ΘNF-Hodge theater: a D-NF-bridge and a D-Θ-bridge sharing the capsule D_J, jointly isomorphic to the model; morphisms are compatible pairs inducing the same bijection of index sets.

IUT1.Rem4_7_2.content: (i) At the level of labels, a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater is summarized by Fig. 4.4: [1 < 2 < ... < l*] for †𝔇_>, (1 2 ... l*) for †𝔇_J, the F_l^*-cycle of ∗'s for †D^⊚ = B(C_K)^0, ⇑ for the D-Θ-bridge, ⇒ for the D-NF-bridge. (ii) The labels from †𝔇_> come from irreducible components of the special fiber (a chain of projective lines) of a tempered covering of a Tate curve ([EtTh] Corollary 2.9), counted additively from an origin: geometric, additive, archimedean, hence Frobenius-like (Corollary 3.8). The ∗'s of †D^⊚ come from primes of a number field permuted cyclically by F_l^* = F_l^×/{±1}: arithmetic, multiplicative, nonarchimedean, hence étale-like. The only common ground is an underlying set of cardinality l*, that of †𝔇_J. (iii) (†ζ_*)^{-1} : J ⥲ LabCusp(†D^⊚) relates arithmetic (elements of J as collections of primes) to geometry (cusps), and may be thought of as a combinatorial Kodaira-Spencer morphism ([HASurI] §1.4).
IUT1.Rem4_7_2.conclusion: Heuristic description of the label structure of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (Fig. 4.4); no new assertion beyond F_l^* = F_l^×/{±1} and the cardinality l* of J.
ambiguities: The classifications (geometric, additive, archimedean versus arithmetic, multiplicative, nonarchimedean) are descriptive, not defined terms.

IUT1.Prop4_8.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) the set of isomorphisms between two D-NF-bridges is an F_l^*-torsor; (ii) the set of isomorphisms between two D-Θ-bridges (respectively two D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters) has cardinality one; (iii) given a D-NF-bridge and a D-Θ-bridge, the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms between their capsules of D-prime-strips that glue them into a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater is an F_l^*-torsor; (iv) given a D-NF-bridge there is a relatively simple functorial algorithm (Examples 4.4 (i), (ii), (iii); 4.5 (i), (ii)) constructing, up to an F_l^*-indeterminacy (by (i), (iii)), a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater whose underlying D-NF-bridge is the given one.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
D-NF-bridges, D-Θ-bridges, D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters as in Definition 4.6
IUT1.Prop4_8.conclusion: (i) F_l^*-torsor of isomorphisms of D-NF-bridges; (ii) unique isomorphism between D-Θ-bridges and between D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters; (iii) F_l^*-torsor of gluings; (iv) a functorial algorithm completing a D-NF-bridge to a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater up to F_l^*-indeterminacy.
obligations: No proof is given; the sentence before the statement (page 114) says it "follows immediately from the definitions". (ii) needs that automorphisms of the model D-Θ-bridge are trivial, which rests on the label rigidity at bad v (Example 4.4) and Proposition 4.2.
D-prime-strips and capsule-full poly-isomorphisms are not in Mathlib.

IUT1.Prop4_9.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) associating to a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater its underlying D-NF-bridge (†D^⊚ ← †𝔇_J) is a natural functor (isomorphisms to isomorphisms) whose output admits an F_l^*-symmetry acting simply transitively on the index set J of the capsule †𝔇_J; (ii) associating the underlying capsule †𝔇_J is a natural functor to the category of l*-capsules of D-prime-strips with capsule-full poly-isomorphisms, whose output admits an S_{l*}-symmetry acting transitively on J; it forgets the labels (the bijection J ⥲ F_l^* of Proposition 4.7 (i)), so that given †𝔇_J only up to isomorphism there are precisely l* possibilities for the label of a given index; (iii) composing (ii) with mono-analyticization (Definition 4.1 (iv)) gives a natural functor to l*-capsules of D^⊢-prime-strips with the same symmetry properties.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
IUT1.Prop4_9.conclusion: Three natural functors with output symmetries F_l^* (simply transitive on J), S_{l*} (transitive on J), and the same for the mono-analytic capsules.
obligations: Proof (page 116): (i), (ii), (iii) "follow immediately from the definitions", with Proposition 4.8 (i) for (i).
ambiguities: As in Proposition 6.8, "symmetry" means an action of a group with a natural outer isomorphism to the named group; for (i) this is not restated on page 115.

IUT1.Rem4_9_1.content: (i) The series will evaluate the étale theta function of [EtTh], in the spirit of the Hodge-Arakelov theory of [HASurI], [HASurII], at the D-prime-strips of †𝔇_J as stipulated by the labels of Proposition 4.7 (i) ([IUTchII] §2), to build arithmetic line bundles whose log-volumes are computed; comparing log-volumes at D-prime-strips with different labels requires the non-labeled outputs of Proposition 4.9 (i), (ii), (iii) (and Proposition 4.11 (i), (ii), via processions, to minimize label indeterminacy). (ii) The F_l^*-symmetry of Proposition 4.9 (i) is transitive and allows comparisons without disturbing the cyclic structure (F_l^*-torsor structure) on J, a combinatorial manifestation of the link to the global object †D^⊚; comparing with D-prime-strips unrelated to J requires forgetting the cyclic structure, which is achieved by the S_{l*}-symmetry of Proposition 4.9 (ii), (iii).
IUT1.Rem4_9_1.conclusion: Motivation for the non-labeled functors of Proposition 4.9 and the processions of Proposition 4.11; no new assertion.

IUT1.Rem4_9_2.content: (i) The indices of the capsule of a D-NF-bridge are synchronized with the labels 1, ..., l*: the correspondence is determined up to the action of an element of F_l^* and is always bijective, a consequence of the number field being represented by a single copy of D^⊚. If instead each D-prime-strip of †𝔇_J had its own copy of D^⊚ (independent globalization) related by a copy of φ^NF_j known only up to F_l^*, and the mutually disjoint F_l^*-translates of V^{±un} ∩ V(K)^bad (whose union is V^Bor ∩ V(K)^bad) were regarded as labeled by F_l^*, each D-prime-strip would carry an independent indeterminacy (Fig. 4.5), and the possible correspondences J → F_l^* would include non-bijective ones. Since F_l^* also acts faithfully on conjugates of the cusp ε, working with V(K) up to F_l^* requires working with conjugates of ε up to F_l^*; nonsynchronized labels are inconsistent with the bijection †ζ_* of Proposition 4.7 (iii). (ii) The single copy of D^⊚ is a single connected component, a single basepoint. (iii) Since F_l^* acts transitively on itself, independent F_l^*- or S_{l*}-indeterminacies at each index give the same set of possibilities. (iv) The synchronized indeterminacy (†ζ_*) is a combinatorial model of a holomorphic structure, the nonsynchronized one of a real analytic structure. (v) Main results of §4: (a) globalizability of labels independent of local structures (Remark 4.3.2 (b), Proposition 4.7 (iii)); (b) comparability of distinct labels (Proposition 4.9, Remark 4.9.1 (i)); (c) absolute comparability (Proposition 4.9 (ii), (iii), Remark 4.9.1 (ii)); (d) minimization of label indeterminacy via processions (Proposition 4.11 (i), (ii)).
explicit_hypotheses: a D-NF-bridge relative to fixed initial Θ-data
IUT1.Rem4_9_2.conclusion: (i) The index-label correspondence of a D-NF-bridge is bijective and determined up to F_l^*; under independent globalization non-bijective correspondences would occur. (ii) to (v): interpretation and summary of §4.
obligations: The synchronization claim of (i) is a restatement of Propositions 4.7, 4.8 (i); the claims about the alternative (independent globalization) are argued informally.
The mutual disjointness of the F_l^*-translates of V^{±un} ∩ V(K)^bad is called manifest, citing Definition 3.1 (f) and Example 4.3 (i).
ambiguities: The alternative scenario of independent globalization in (i) is described but not defined precisely (pages 117 to 118).

IUT1.Rem4_9_3.content: (i) Applying the mono-anabelian theory of [AbsTopIII] to the local and global arithmetic fundamental groups of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater ([IUTchIII]) requires the geometric fundamental groups inside the isomorphs of Π_{C_K}, Π_v, not only the absolute Galois groups: the outer Galois action on the geometric fundamental group is what allows ring structures to be reconstructed compatibly with localization and globalization (Fig. 4.3); [AbsTopIII] Remark 5.10.3 (i) compares this entrusting of arithmetic moduli with the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism of an indigenous bundle. (ii) This explains why D_v is defined in Examples 3.3, 3.4 via the arrow-decorated X_v rather than C_v (Remark 4.2.1): with C_v, the primes v, w of Remark 4.2.1, taken as v, v' of Fig. 4.3, would by compatibility with localization and globalization lead to nonsynchronized labels (Remark 4.9.2 (i), Fig. 4.5), incompatible with the bijection of Proposition 4.7 (iii).
IUT1.Rem4_9_3.conclusion: Justification for using X_v (arrow decoration) rather than C_v in Examples 3.3, 3.4: the alternative would conflict with the bijection †ζ_* of Proposition 4.7 (iii).
obligations: The claim in (ii) that using C_v leads to nonsynchronized labels is argued "at a combinatorial level" by reference to Remarks 4.2.1 and 4.9.2; it is not derived formally.
ambiguities: Page 119 writes "the crucial bijection †ζ of Proposition 4.7 (iii)" without the subscript used in Proposition 4.7; read as †ζ_* (suspected misprint).

IUT1.Def4_10.content: For a category C and a positive integer n, an n-procession (procession of length n) of C is a diagram P_1 ↪ P_2 ↪ ... ↪ P_n in which each P_j (j = 1, ..., n) is a j-capsule of objects of C and each arrow P_j ↪ P_{j+1} denotes the collection of all capsule-full poly-morphisms from P_j to P_{j+1}. A morphism from an n-procession (P_1 ↪ ... ↪ P_n) to an m-procession (Q_1 ↪ ... ↪ Q_m) is an order-preserving injection ι : {1, ..., n} ↪ {1, ..., m} (so n ≤ m) together with a capsule-full poly-morphism P_j ↪ Q_{ι(j)} for each j = 1, ..., n.
explicit_hypotheses: C a category
n a positive integer
IUT1.Def4_10.conclusion: Definition of n-processions of C and their morphisms (Fig. 4.6 shows an l*-procession of D-prime-strips).
obligations: Definition. Unlike most objects of IUT I, it uses only categories, capsules and capsule-full poly-morphisms (§0), so it could be stated in Lean on top of the existing §0 definitions.
ambiguities: The text does not state how morphisms of processions compose; composition of order-preserving injections and of capsule-full poly-morphisms is the evident candidate.
Whether the P_j are required to be related to each other beyond the arrows (for example, subcapsules) is not stated in the definition; in Proposition 4.11 they are subcapsules of one capsule.

IUT1.Prop4_11.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) given a D-Θ-bridge †φ^Θ_* : †𝔇_J → †𝔇_>, let Prc(†𝔇_J) be the l*-procession of D-prime-strips formed by the subcapsules of †𝔇_J corresponding to S*_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ S*_j = {1, 2, ..., j} ⊆ ... ⊆ S*_{l*} = F_l^* (positive integers standing for their images in F_l^*), relative to †χ : J ⥲ F_l^* of Proposition 4.7 (i). Then †φ^Θ_* ↦ Prc(†𝔇_J) is a natural functor from D-Θ-bridges and their isomorphisms to processions of D-prime-strips and their morphisms, whose output has, for each n ∈ {1, ..., l*}, precisely n possibilities for the element of F_l^* corresponding to a given index of the n-capsule; taking the product over F_l^*, the indeterminacy of (l*)^{(l*)} possibilities of Proposition 4.9 (ii) is reduced to l*! possibilities (also after pre-composing with †HT^{D-ΘNF} ↦ †φ^Θ_*). (ii) Composing with mono-analyticization gives a natural functor †φ^Θ_* ↦ Prc(†𝔇^⊢_J) to processions of D^⊢-prime-strips with the same indeterminacy properties.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
a D-Θ-bridge †φ^Θ_* : †𝔇_J → †𝔇_> (Definition 4.6 (ii))
IUT1.Prop4_11.conclusion: Natural functors to l*-processions of D- and D^⊢-prime-strips, with label indeterminacy n at the n-th capsule and total indeterminacy l*! instead of (l*)^{(l*)}.
obligations: Proof (page 121): (i), (ii) "follow immediately from the definitions".
The counting step ∏_{n=1}^{l*} n = l*! versus (l*)^{(l*)} is elementary and could be checked in Lean on its own.
ambiguities: The phrase "precisely n possibilities" counts possibilities prior to applying the functor; the formal meaning of a set of possibilities is not defined.
