IUT1.Cor4_12.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) the composite functor †HT^{D-ΘNF} ↦ †𝔇_> ↦ †𝔇^⊢_> (mono-analyticization of the codomain of the underlying D-Θ-bridge) goes from D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters and their isomorphisms to D^⊢-prime-strips and their isomorphisms; for D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters †HT, ‡HT the D-ΘNF-link †HT →(D) ‡HT is defined as the full poly-isomorphism †𝔇^⊢_> ⥲ ‡𝔇^⊢_>. (ii) For an infinite chain ... →(D) ^{n}HT^{D-ΘNF} →(D) ^{n+1}HT^{D-ΘNF} →(D) ... (n ∈ Z) of D-ΘNF-linked theaters, one obtains a chain of full poly-isomorphisms ... ⥲ ^n𝔇^⊢_> ⥲ ^{n+1}𝔇^⊢_> ⥲ ...; the output of (i) is a constant invariant, a mono-analytic core, of the chain. (iii) Regarding each theater of the chain as a spoke from this core gives the étale-picture of D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters (Fig. 4.7), which admits arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (the labels n ∈ Z).
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
(ii), (iii): an infinite chain of D-ΘNF-linked D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters indexed by n ∈ Z
IUT1.Cor4_12.conclusion: Definition of the D-ΘNF-link as a full poly-isomorphism of D^⊢-prime-strips; the resulting chain of full poly-isomorphisms makes †𝔇^⊢_> a constant invariant (mono-analytic core); the étale-picture admits arbitrary permutation symmetries of the spokes.
obligations: No proof is given; the sentence before the statement (page 121) calls it "an immediate consequence of our discussion".

"Constant invariant" and "arbitrary permutation symmetries" must be given a precise meaning (for instance, a functor from the chain category that factors through a point up to the full poly-isomorphisms, and an action of the permutation group of Z on the diagram) before the statement can be formalized.
ambiguities: "Constant invariant" and "mono-analytic core" (page 122) are explained by reference to Remarks 3.8.1 (ii) and 3.9.1, not defined.

IUT1.Ex5_1.content: Global Frobenioids attached to the D-NF-bridge portion of a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater †HT^{D-ΘNF} (Definition 4.6). From π1(†D^⊚) one constructs group-theoretically, via [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 applied through the Θ-approach of Remark 3.1.2, an isomorph M^⊛(†D^⊚) of F̄^× with its field structure, the category †D^⊛ (B(−)^0 of a profinite group corresponding to C_{F_mod}) with a natural morphism †D^⊚ → †D^⊛, monoids of κ-, ∞κ-, ∞κ×-coric rational functions, the quotient π1^rat → π1^{κ-sol}, and a poly-action of F_l^* (parts (i), (ii)); a Frobenioid †F^⊛ over †D^⊛ with its restrictions †F^⊚ and †F^⊛_mod (part (iii)); birationalizations, local monoids O^▷_p and decomposition groups (part (iv)); ∞κ-coric and ∞κ×-coric structures and their uniqueness, and the reconstruction of Prime(†F^⊛_mod) ⥲ V_mod (part (v)); the same for †F^⊚, †D^⊚ (part (vi)); copies †F^⊛_j, the diagonal †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} and products over the capsule index set J, with realifications (part (vii)).
explicit_hypotheses: †HT^{D-ΘNF} = (†D^⊚ ← †D_J → †D_>) a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater (Definition 4.6), relative to a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (F̄/F, X_F, l, C_K, V, V^bad_mod, ε) as in Definition 3.1 (page 123)
implicit_hypotheses: Only the D-NF-bridge portion †φ^NF_* is used (Remark 5.1.2).
IUT1.Ex5_1.conclusion: Group-theoretic or category-theoretic constructions of the global Frobenioids †F^⊛, †F^⊚, †F^⊛_mod and their associated monoids and structures, together with the asserted properties of parts (i) to (vii): the κ-sol-conjugate synchronization of part (i), the uniqueness up to a uniquely determined isomorphism of the ∞κ-coric (respectively ∞κ×-coric) structure on †F^⊛ in part (v), and the functorial reconstruction algorithms of part (v).
external_dependencies: [FrdI] Theorem 5.2, Example 6.3, Corollary 4.11, Theorem 6.4, Proposition 4.4, Proposition 5.3
obligations: Construct the objects of parts (i) to (vii) and prove the properties asserted in parts (i) and (v); the text derives them from [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9, [AbsTopII] Corollary 3.3 and [FrdI], with phrases such as "it follows formally" and "it follows immediately".
Part (vi) is left to the reader as routine.
ambiguities: Example 5.1 mixes definitions (notation and constructions) with assertions (uniqueness and reconstruction); the assertions are recorded in the child records .i and .v.

IUT1.Ex5_1.i.content: From π1(†D^⊚), via [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 and the Θ-approach, one constructs group-theoretically M^⊛(†D^⊚) (an isomorph of F̄^×) with its π1(†D^⊚)-action and field structure on M̄^⊛ = M^⊛ ∪ {0}; a profinite group corresponding to C_{F_mod} containing π1(†D^⊚) as an open subgroup, whose B(−)^0 is written †D^⊛, with a natural morphism †D^⊚ → †D^⊛; the invariants M^⊛_mod ⊆ M^⊛ and M̄^⊛_mod ⊆ M̄^⊛ (corresponding to F^×_mod ⊆ F̄^× and F_mod ⊆ F̄); a group π1^rat(†D^⊛) (absolute Galois group of the function field of C_{F_mod}) surjecting onto π1(†D^⊛); pseudo-monoids M^⊛_κ, M^⊛_{∞κ}, M^⊛_{∞κ×} of κ-, ∞κ-, ∞κ×-coric rational functions; a quotient π1^rat(†D^⊛) ↠ π1^{κ-sol}(†D^⊛) with kernel π1^{rat/κ-sol}(†D^⊛) and pseudo-monoids M^⊛_{∞κ}, M^⊛_{κ-sol}, M^⊛_sol with π1^{κ-sol}-actions; subgroups Aut^SL_ε(†D^⊚) ⊆ Aut^SL(†D^⊚) ⊆ Aut(†D^⊚) and natural isomorphisms Aut^SL/Aut^SL_ε ⥲ Aut/Aut_ε ⥲ F_l^*, a poly-action of F_l^* on †D^⊚.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1
IUT1.Ex5_1.i.conclusion: With π1^rat(†D^⊚) = π1^rat(†D^⊛) ×_{π1(†D^⊛)} π1(†D^⊚) and π1^{rat/κ-sol}(†D^⊚) = π1^{rat/κ-sol}(†D^⊛) ∩ π1^rat(†D^⊚): the poly-action of F_l^* on π1^rat(†D^⊚), regarded as arising from elements of Aut^SL(†D^⊚), is well defined up to π1^{rat/κ-sol}(†D^⊚)-conjugacy, and the induced poly-action on the κ-sol-outer representation π1^{κ-sol}(†D^⊛) → Out^{κ-sol}(π1^{rat/κ-sol}(†D^⊚)) is well defined without conjugacy indeterminacies and equal to the trivial action. This is called κ-sol-conjugate synchronization.
obligations: The constructions rest on [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 and [AbsTopII] Corollary 3.3.
The synchronization claim is said to "follow formally" from the linear disjointness property of Remark 3.1.7 (iii); a formalization must derive it.
ambiguities: Page 124: the poly-action of F_l^* on π1^rat(†D^⊚) is only well defined up to conjugation by elements of π1^rat(†D^⊚) itself; the claim of page 125 is about the induced action on the outer representation, not on π1^rat(†D^⊚).

IUT1.Ex5_1.ii.content: The field structure on M̄^⊛(†D^⊚) gives the set of valuations V(†D^⊚) (an analogue of V(F̄)) with its π1(†D^⊚)-action, hence a monoid Φ^⊛(†D^⊚)(−) on †D^⊛ assigning to each object A the monoid of stack-theoretic arithmetic divisors on the corresponding subfield M̄^⊛(†D^⊚)^A, with natural morphisms M^⊛(†D^⊚)^A → Φ^⊛(†D^⊚)(A)^gp. By [FrdI] Theorem 5.2 (ii) this data determines a model Frobenioid F^⊛(†D^⊚) over †D^⊛.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1 and the constructions of IUT1.Ex5_1.i
IUT1.Ex5_1.ii.conclusion: Construction: a model Frobenioid F^⊛(†D^⊚) over the base category †D^⊛, built from V(†D^⊚) and the monoid Φ^⊛(†D^⊚)(−).
obligations: The existence of the model Frobenioid is [FrdI] Theorem 5.2 (ii); Frobenioids are not in Mathlib.

IUT1.Ex5_1.iii.content: Let †F^⊛ be any category equivalent to F^⊛(†D^⊚); it carries a natural Frobenioid structure. Given a morphism †D^⊚ → Base(†F^⊛) abstractly equivalent to the natural morphism †D^⊚ → †D^⊛, the resulting isomorphism Base(†F^⊛) ⥲ †D^⊛ (uniquely determined, by F-coricity of C_F and [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9) identifies Base(†F^⊛) with †D^⊛. Define †F^⊚ as the restriction of †F^⊛ to †D^⊚, and †F^⊛_mod as the restriction to the full subcategory of terminal objects of †D^⊛. When † arises from Definition 3.1 data, †F^⊛_mod may be thought of as the Frobenioid of arithmetic line bundles on the stack S_mod of Remark 3.1.5.
explicit_hypotheses: †F^⊛ a category equivalent to F^⊛(†D^⊚)
a morphism †D^⊚ → Base(†F^⊛) abstractly equivalent (§0) to the natural morphism †D^⊚ → †D^⊛
IUT1.Ex5_1.iii.conclusion: Definitions of †F^⊚ and †F^⊛_mod ⊆ †F^⊛; the identification Base(†F^⊛) = †D^⊛ is asserted to be uniquely determined.
obligations: Uniqueness of the isomorphism Base(†F^⊛) ⥲ †D^⊛ is justified by F-coricity of C_F and [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9.
ambiguities: The phrase "thought of as the Frobenioid of arithmetic line bundles on S_mod" (page 126) is an interpretation, not a definition.

IUT1.Ex5_1.iv.content: Birationalizations (superscript birat) of †F^⊚, †F^⊛, †F^⊛_mod are category-theoretic. For A ∈ Ob(†F^⊛), O^×(A^birat) is the multiplicative group of the corresponding finite extension of F_mod; letting A range over Frobenius-trivial objects over Galois objects of †D^⊛ gives a pair π1(†D^⊛) ↷ Õ^{⊛×}, up to inner automorphisms. For a prime p of the divisor monoid Φ_{†F^⊛}(A), the inverse image of the subset given by p under O^×(A^birat) → Φ(A)^gp determines a submonoid O^▷_p (integral elements for the valuation of p), with units O^×_p. For p_0 a prime over a terminal object, the elements of Aut(A) fixing O^▷_p give a closed subgroup Π_{p_0} ⊆ π1(†D^⊛), well defined up to conjugation: the decomposition group of some v ∈ V_mod.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1.iii
IUT1.Ex5_1.iv.conclusion: Category-theoretic constructions of the pair π1(†D^⊛) ↷ Õ^{⊛×}, of the submonoids O^▷_p, O^×_p, and of the decomposition groups Π_{p_0}; moreover p_0 is nonarchimedean if and only if the p-cohomological dimension of Π_{p_0} is 3 for infinitely many primes p (citing [NSW] Theorem 7.1.8 (i)).
obligations: Category-theoreticity of the birationalization, the divisor monoid and Frobenius-trivial objects is cited from [FrdI]; the criterion for nonarchimedean primes is cited from [NSW].

IUT1.Ex5_1.v.content: Write π1(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛ for the pair of (iv), and †M^⊛_sol, †M^⊛_mod for its π1^{rat/κ-sol}-, π1^rat-invariants. An ∞κ-coric (respectively ∞κ×-coric) structure on †F^⊛ is a pair π1^rat(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ} (respectively ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ×}) isomorphic, as a pseudo-monoid with continuous action, to π1^rat(†D^⊛) ↷ M^⊛_{∞κ}(†D^⊚) (respectively M^⊛_{∞κ×}(†D^⊚)) of (i). Using Kummer classes into lim H^1(H, μ_Ẑ(−)), with μ_Ẑ(−) = Hom(Q/Z, −), and the cyclotome μ^Θ_Ẑ(π1(†D^⊚)) of the Θ-approach.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1.iv
an ∞κ-coric (respectively ∞κ×-coric) structure on †F^⊛ (page 127)
IUT1.Ex5_1.v.conclusion: (a) Using Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1} inside Ẑ ⊗ Q, there is a unique isomorphism of cyclotomes μ^Θ_Ẑ(π1(†D^⊚)) ⥲ μ_Ẑ(†M^⊛_{∞κ}) (respectively μ_Ẑ(†M^⊛_{∞κ×})) inducing an isomorphism M^⊛_{∞κ}(†D^⊚) ⥲ †M^⊛_{∞κ} (respectively for ∞κ×), and a unique isomorphism of cyclotomes μ^Θ_Ẑ(π1(†D^⊚)) ⥲ μ_Ẑ(†M^⊛) inducing isomorphisms M^⊛ ⥲ †M^⊛, M^⊛_sol ⥲ †M^⊛_sol, M^⊛_mod ⥲ †M^⊛_mod compatible with the integral submonoids O^▷_p. (b) Hence †F^⊛ always admits an ∞κ-coric (respectively ∞κ×-coric) structure, unique up to a uniquely determined isomorphism (page 128). (c) Any ∞κ×-coric structure determines an ∞κ-coric structure by the torsion condition on restricted Kummer classes at decomposition groups of strictly critical points of C_{F_mod}; restricting Kummer classes to decomposition groups of noncritical F_mod- and F_sol-valued points gives a functorial algorithm reconstructing †M^⊛_mod, †M^⊛_sol with field structure and valuations (page 129), and similarly with π1^rat, F̄ and †M^⊛ substituted. (d) A category-theoretic natural bijection Prime(†F^⊛_mod) ⥲ V_mod, and for nonarchimedean p_0 a pair Π_{p_0} ↷ Ô^▷_{p_0} of completions, which is an MLF-Galois TM-pair of strictly Belyi type ([AbsTopIII] Definition 3.1 (ii)) (pages 129 to 130).
obligations: The text says the unique cyclotome isomorphisms and the uniqueness of the ∞κ-coric structure "follow immediately" from [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9 (d) and the observation Q_{>0} ∩ Ẑ^× = {1}; a formalization needs the Kummer injectivity and the reconstruction of [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9.
The reconstruction of †M^⊛_mod, †M^⊛_sol (page 129) is said to follow immediately from Remark 3.1.7 (i) to (iii), [AbsTopII] Corollary 3.3 (iii) and [AbsTopIII] Theorem 1.9.
ambiguities: Page 127: the π1^rat-action in an ∞κ-coric structure factors through π1^{κ-sol}, while that of an ∞κ×-coric structure does not; the parallel "respectively" clauses must be read with that difference in mind.

IUT1.Ex5_1.vi.content: The discussion of (iv) and (v) for †F^⊛, †D^⊛ may also be carried out for †F^⊚, †D^⊚.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1.iv and IUT1.Ex5_1.v
IUT1.Ex5_1.vi.conclusion: The analogues of (iv) and (v) hold for †F^⊚ over †D^⊚.
obligations: The text leaves "the routine details to the reader".

IUT1.Ex5_1.vii.content: For the index set J of the capsule †D_J, put V_j = {v_j} (v ∈ V), with natural bijections V_j ⥲ V; the diagonal subset V_{⟨J⟩} ⊆ V_J = ∏_{j∈J} V_j also maps bijectively to V. This gives bijections V_{⟨J⟩} ⥲ V_j ⥲ Prime(†F^⊛_mod) ⥲ V_mod. Define †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} = {†F^⊛_mod, V_{⟨J⟩} ⥲ Prime(†F^⊛_mod)} and †F^⊛_j = {†F^⊛_mod, V_j ⥲ Prime(†F^⊛_mod)}, copies of †F^⊛_mod situated on the constituent labeled j, respectively diagonally on all constituents; there is a natural embedding of categories †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} ↪ †F^⊛_J = ∏_{j∈J} †F^⊛_j. Realifications †F^{⊛R}_j, †F^{⊛R}_{⟨J⟩}, †F^{⊛R}_J = ∏ †F^{⊛R}_j are defined via [FrdI] Proposition 5.3.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1.v
J the index set of the capsule of D-prime-strips †D_J
IUT1.Ex5_1.vii.conclusion: Definitions of †F^⊛_j, †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩}, †F^⊛_J and their realifications; the category †F^⊛_J is not regarded as equipped with a Frobenioid structure.
ambiguities: By abuse of notation, †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} also denotes the underlying category of the pair (page 130).

IUT1.Rem5_1_1.content: †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} may be viewed as the Frobenioid of divisors on V_J (finite formal sums with Z or R coefficients) that are constant in j ∈ J, constant distributions as in Fig. 5.1; the product of the underlying categories of the †F^⊛_j corresponds to arbitrary distributions on V_J.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_1.vii
IUT1.Rem5_1_1.conclusion: Interpretation: †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} corresponds to constant distributions on V_J and ∏_j †F^⊛_j to arbitrary distributions.
ambiguities: Heuristic description ("may be thought of"); no assertion requiring proof.

IUT1.Rem5_1_2.content: The constructions of Example 5.1 use only the D-NF-bridge portion †φ^NF_* of the D-ΘNF-Hodge theater †HT^{D-ΘNF}.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_1
IUT1.Rem5_1_2.conclusion: Example 5.1 depends only on the D-NF-bridge †φ^NF_*.
obligations: Check, once Example 5.1 is formalized, that its constructions take only the D-NF-bridge as input; the text calls this manifest.

IUT1.Rem5_1_3.content: Kummer theory in the sense of [FrdII] Definition 2.1 (ii) can be performed with †F^⊚, †F^⊛, †M^⊛, †M^⊛_sol, †M^⊛_{∞κ}, †M^⊛_{∞κ×}, †M^⊛_{κ-sol} (Kummer-ready), but not with †F^⊛_mod, †M^⊛_mod, †M^⊛_κ (Kummer-blind), since elements of F^×_mod or κ-coric functions need not admit N-th roots. The additive (ring or field) structure on the birational monoid portion of †F^⊛_mod can only be recovered given the extra datum of the natural embedding †F^⊛_mod ↪ †F^⊛; without it, †F^⊛_mod is subject to a Kummer black-out. The copies †F^⊛_j, †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩}, †F^⊛_J of Example 5.1 (vii) are also Kummer-blind.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_1 (v) to (vii)
IUT1.Rem5_1_3.conclusion: Terminology (Kummer-ready, Kummer-blind) and the assertion that the additive structure on the birational monoid portion of †F^⊛_mod may only be recovered from the embedding †F^⊛_mod ↪ †F^⊛, via the rigidity properties of Corollary 5.3 (i).
obligations: The statement "may only be recovered" is a negative claim; the text gives no argument that no other recovery exists.
ambiguities: "May only be recovered" (page 131) may be read as a claim about the constructions of this paper rather than a mathematical impossibility statement.

IUT1.Rem5_1_4.content: The reconstruction algorithms for number fields of Example 5.1 rest on Belyi cuspidalization ([AbsTopIII] §1), whose viewpoint is that elements of number fields can be expressed geometrically by Belyi maps; the rest of [AbsTopIII] (especially §5) is a theory of analytic continuation of these functions under the logarithm maps at the localizations. The remark relates this to Remarks 4.3.2, 4.3.3 and, as an arithmetic analogue, to hyperbolic analytic continuations on the upper half-plane in the Motivating Example of [GeoAnbd], comparing the inequality ≤ 1 for derivatives with the decreasing degrees used to construct Belyi maps.
IUT1.Rem5_1_4.conclusion: Heuristic commentary; no mathematical assertion requiring proof.

IUT1.Rem5_1_5.content: Consequence of κ-sol-conjugate synchronization: the Kummer theory of π1^{κ-sol}(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ}, of †M^⊛_mod and of π1^{κ-sol}(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_sol (abstract analogues of ∞κ-coric functions, F^×_mod, F^×_sol) can be performed compatibly, without conjugacy indeterminacies, with the poly-action of (Aut^SL(†D^⊚) ↠) F_l^*. The remark then argues that a solvable-Uchida-type reconstruction of ring structure would be meaningless for the theory, being incompatible with the localization operations in a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater, since absolute Galois groups of nonarchimedean completions have automorphisms not arising from field automorphisms ([NSW], Closing Remark before Theorem 12.2.7); and that the outer action of the absolute Galois group of a number field on the geometric fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve does not factor through its maximal solvable quotient, as a formal consequence of [NodNon] Theorem C.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_1
IUT1.Rem5_1_5.conclusion: (1) The κ-sol Kummer theory of Example 5.1 (v) is compatible, without conjugacy indeterminacies, with the poly-action of F_l^*. (2) The outer Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve over a number field admits no solvable factorization.
obligations: Claim (1) rests on the synchronization of Example 5.1 (i); claim (2) is said to be a formal consequence of the Galois injectivity result [NodNon] Theorem C.
ambiguities: The assessment that a solvable-Uchida-type reconstruction is "meaningless" for the theory is a methodological judgment, not a mathematical statement.

IUT1.Def5_2.content: F-prime-strips {F_v}: at nonarchimedean v a Frobenioid equivalent to the model, at archimedean v a triple with Kummer structure; F^⊢-prime-strips; morphisms are collections of isomorphisms; F^⊩-prime-strips (C^⊩, Prime(C^⊩) ⥲ V, F^⊢, {ρ_v}); parts (v) to (viii) on ∞κ-coric and κ-coric structures, including the Kummer structure cyclotomic isomorphism at archimedean v.

IUT1.Rem5_2_1.content: Notation: 𝔉 denotes an F-prime-strip (fraktur in the paper). (i) There is a functorial algorithm constructing D- (respectively D^⊢-) prime-strips from F- (respectively F^⊢-) prime-strips. (ii) There is a functorial algorithm 𝔉 ↦ 𝔉^⊢ = {F^⊢_v}, the mono-analyticization of 𝔉; and, using the simple structure of C^⊩_mod (copies of R_{≥0} indexed by V ⥲ V_mod, related by a product formula) and the rigidity of the divisor monoids of the Frobenioids at each v of an F-prime-strip (especially the topological field structure of A_{D_v} of Example 3.4 (i)), a functorial algorithm 𝔉 ↦ 𝔉^⊩ = (C^⊩, Prime(C^⊩) ⥲ V, 𝔉^⊢, {ρ_v}) producing an F^⊩-prime-strip isomorphic to 𝔉^⊩_mod of Example 3.5 (ii).
explicit_hypotheses: 𝔉 = {F_v}_{v∈V} an F-prime-strip (respectively 𝔉^⊢ an F^⊢-prime-strip) in the sense of Definition 5.2 (i), (ii)
IUT1.Rem5_2_1.conclusion: (i) Functorial algorithms F-prime-strip ↦ D-prime-strip and F^⊢-prime-strip ↦ D^⊢-prime-strip. (ii) Functorial algorithms 𝔉 ↦ 𝔉^⊢ and 𝔉 ↦ 𝔉^⊩, the latter producing an F^⊩-prime-strip (Definition 5.2 (iv)).
obligations: The text says each algorithm "follows immediately" from Definitions 4.1, 5.2 and Examples 3.2 to 3.5 (items cited by part number); a formalization must construct the algorithms and prove functoriality.
ambiguities: "Roughly speaking" (page 143) qualifies the description of C^⊩_mod; the precise object is that of Example 3.5.

IUT1.Rem5_2_2.content: In the terminology of Remark 5.1.3, F-prime-strips are Kummer-ready (at nonarchimedean v, by [FrdII] §2), while F^⊢-prime-strips are Kummer-blind.
IUT1.Rem5_2_2.conclusion: Classification: F-prime-strips are Kummer-ready, F^⊢-prime-strips Kummer-blind.
ambiguities: Kummer-ready and Kummer-blind are informal labels (Remark 5.1.3), not defined predicates.

IUT1.Rem5_2_3.content: In constructing ∞κ-coric structures from ∞κ×-coric structures (Definition 5.2 (vi)) at v ∈ V^bad, it is natural to take the decomposition groups of strictly critical points to be those of the point of C_v that is the image of the zero-labeled evaluation points (label 0 ∈ |F_l|, Example 4.4 (i)); in the notation of Example 4.4 (i) this is the image of the point μ_−.
explicit_hypotheses: v ∈ V^bad
IUT1.Rem5_2_3.conclusion: A recommended choice: the strictly critical point used at bad v is the image in C_v of the zero-labeled evaluation points, equivalently of μ_−.
obligations: A formalization of Definition 5.2 (vi) at bad v must fix this choice of decomposition groups.
ambiguities: "It is natural to take" (page 143) leaves open whether the choice is part of the definition or a convention.

IUT1.Cor5_3.content: (i) Isom of the global Frobenioids to Isom of their bases is bijective. (ii) Isom of F-prime-strips to Isom of the associated D-prime-strips is bijective. (iii) For F^⊢-prime-strips the map is surjective. (iv) Aut(F_v) → Aut(D_v) is bijective at bad v.
IUT1.Cor5_3.conclusion: Reconstruction of Frobenioid data from base data.

IUT1.Rem5_3_1.content: (i) In the situation of Corollary 5.3 (ii), let φ : ¹𝔇 → ²𝔇 be a morphism of D-prime-strips (not necessarily an isomorphism) inducing isomorphisms at v ∈ V^good and an isomorphism φ^⊢ : ¹𝔇^⊢ ⥲ ²𝔇^⊢ of the associated D^⊢-prime-strips. The pull-back (categorical fiber product) of the Frobenioids of ²𝔉 along the components of φ gives a pulled-back F-prime-strip φ*(²𝔉) whose associated D-prime-strip is tautologically equal to ¹𝔇; by Corollary 5.3 (ii) this equality determines a unique isomorphism ¹𝔉 ⥲ φ*(²𝔉). The arrow ψ : ¹𝔉 → ²𝔉 is defined as the pair (φ, ¹𝔉 ⥲ φ*(²𝔉)), the morphism uniquely determined by φ, said to lie over φ. (ii) The same conventions apply to poly-morphisms; details are left to the reader.
explicit_hypotheses: ¹𝔉, ²𝔉 F-prime-strips with associated D-prime-strips ¹𝔇, ²𝔇
φ : ¹𝔇 → ²𝔇 a morphism of D-prime-strips inducing isomorphisms at all v ∈ V^good and an isomorphism of the associated D^⊢-prime-strips
IUT1.Rem5_3_1.conclusion: Definition of the arrow ψ : ¹𝔉 → ²𝔉 lying over φ, together with the claims that φ*(²𝔉) is an F-prime-strip with associated D-prime-strip ¹𝔇 and that the isomorphism ¹𝔉 ⥲ φ*(²𝔉) is unique.
obligations: Show that the pull-back is an F-prime-strip (the text says this "follows immediately" from the constructions and [AbsTopIII] Proposition 3.2 (iv)); uniqueness follows from Corollary 5.3 (ii).
Part (ii) on poly-morphisms is left to the reader.
ambiguities: At bad v, φ need not be an isomorphism; the pull-back of the tempered Frobenioid along such a component is used without a separate construction on these pages.

IUT1.Rem5_3_2.content: As with Corollary 5.3 (i), (ii), the rigidity property of Corollary 5.3 (iv) may be regarded as essentially a consequence of the Kummer-readiness of the tempered Frobenioid F_v (double underline) at bad v; compare the proofs of [AbsTopIII] Proposition 3.2 (iv) and Corollary 5.2 (iv).
IUT1.Rem5_3_2.conclusion: Interpretation of Corollary 5.3 (iv) as a consequence of Kummer-readiness; no new assertion.

IUT1.Rem5_3_3.content: Correction to [FrdI]: the hypothesis of unit-profinite type in [FrdI] Proposition 5.6 (hence in [FrdI] Corollary 5.7 (iii)) may be removed. In the notation of the proof of [FrdI] Proposition 5.6, writing φ'_p = c_p·φ_p with c_p ∈ O^×(A) for p ∈ Primes, the commutation φ'_2·φ'_p = φ'_p·φ'_2 gives c_2·c_p^2·φ_2·φ_p = c_p·c_2^p·φ_2·φ_p, so c_2·c_p^2 = c_p·c_2^p, that is c_p = c_2^{p−1}; hence φ'_p = c_2^{-1}·φ_p·c_2, and taking u = c_2^{-1} removes the last two paragraphs of that proof.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of the proof of [FrdI] Proposition 5.6: Frobenius-type endomorphisms φ_p, φ'_p = c_p·φ_p with c_p ∈ O^×(A), for p ∈ Primes
implicit_hypotheses: φ_p·c = c^p·φ_p for c ∈ O^×(A) (used in the displayed computation)
O^×(A) is commutative and cancellative, so that c_2·c_p^2 = c_p·c_2^p can be solved for c_p
φ'_2 and φ'_p commute, and the φ_p commute
IUT1.Rem5_3_3.conclusion: c_p = c_2^{p−1} and φ'_p = c_2^{-1}·φ_p·c_2 for every prime p; consequently [FrdI] Proposition 5.6 and Corollary 5.7 (iii) hold without the unit-profinite hypothesis.
obligations: The displayed computation (page 146) is an elementary identity in a monoid with the stated commutation rule and could be checked in Lean on its own; the conclusion about [FrdI] Proposition 5.6 needs that proof.
ambiguities: The implicit hypotheses are inferred from the displayed computation; the rule φ_p·c = c^p·φ_p is not stated on page 146.

IUT1.Ex5_4.content: Model Θ- and NF-bridges. Notation: 𝔉 and 𝔇 denote F- and D-prime-strips (fraktur in the paper). Given a Θ-Hodge theater †HT^Θ whose associated D-prime-strip equals †𝔇_> (page 146), †𝔉_> is the F-prime-strip tautologically associated to it (page 147). Parts: (i) copies †𝔉_j (j ∈ J) over †𝔇_j, a diagonal †𝔉_{⟨J⟩}, the capsule †𝔉_J, and the diagonal arrow; (ii) poly-morphisms †ψ^Θ_j : †𝔉_j → †𝔉_> uniquely determined by †φ^Θ_j and their collection †ψ^Θ_*; (iii) δ-valuations; (iv) the localization †F^⊚|_δ, poly-morphisms to †F^⊚, and their compatibility with ∞κ-coric structures; (v) the unique †ψ^NF_* lying over †φ^NF_*; (vi) restriction functors and realifications; (vii) pivotal distributions.
explicit_hypotheses: the D-ΘNF-Hodge theater †HT^{D-ΘNF} and initial Θ-data of Section 5 (page 123)
a Θ-Hodge theater †HT^Θ (Definition 3.6) whose associated D-prime-strip is equal to †𝔇_> (pages 146 to 147)
IUT1.Ex5_4.conclusion: Constructions of the model Θ-bridge data (†𝔉_J, †ψ^Θ_*, †𝔉_>) and model NF-bridge data (†𝔉_J, †ψ^NF_*, †F^⊚, †F^⊛), with the asserted uniqueness statements of parts (ii) and (v) and the independence statement of part (vi).
obligations: Construct the objects of parts (i) to (vii); the uniqueness claims rest on Corollary 5.3 (ii), the localization of part (iv) on [SemiAnbd] Theorem 6.6 (bad v) and [AbsTopIII] Corollaries 2.8, 2.9 (archimedean v).
Frobenioids and prime-strips are not in Mathlib.
ambiguities: †F^⊚|_δ is only well defined up to isomorphism (page 148), because V^{±un} → V_mod is not injective; poly-morphisms ‡𝔉 → †F^⊚ are therefore defined as full poly-isomorphisms to †F^⊚|_δ for some δ.

IUT1.Ex5_4.i.content: For j ∈ J, †𝔉_j = {†F_{v_j}} is an F-prime-strip whose associated D-prime-strip is †𝔇_j; †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} is an F-prime-strip with associated D-prime-strip †𝔇_{⟨J⟩}; †𝔉_J = ∏_{j∈J} †𝔉_j, the formal product denoting the capsule with index set J. †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} relates to †𝔉_> by the full poly-isomorphism †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} ⥲ †𝔉_> and to †𝔉_J by the diagonal arrow whose j-component is the full poly-isomorphism †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} ⥲ †𝔉_j.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_4
IUT1.Ex5_4.i.conclusion: Definitions of †𝔉_j, †𝔉_{⟨J⟩}, †𝔉_J and of the diagonal arrow †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} → †𝔉_J.

IUT1.Ex5_4.ii.content: Besides the full poly-isomorphism †𝔉_> ⥲ †𝔉_j, †𝔉_> is related to †𝔉_j by the poly-morphism †ψ^Θ_j : †𝔉_j → †𝔉_> uniquely determined by †φ^Θ_j as in Remark 5.3.1; †ψ^Θ_* : †𝔉_J → †𝔉_> denotes the collection {†ψ^Θ_j}_{j∈J}, lying over †φ^Θ_* = {†φ^Θ_j}_{j∈J}.
explicit_hypotheses: the setting of IUT1.Ex5_4.i
IUT1.Ex5_4.ii.conclusion: Definition of †ψ^Θ_*, with the claim that each †ψ^Θ_j is uniquely determined by †φ^Θ_j.
obligations: Uniqueness rests on Remark 5.3.1 and Corollary 5.3 (ii); Remark 5.3.1 (ii) leaves the poly-morphism case to the reader.

IUT1.Ex5_4.iii.content: For δ ∈ LabCusp(†D^⊚) there is a unique Aut_ε(†D^⊚)-orbit of isomorphisms †D^⊚ ⥲ D^⊚ mapping δ ↦ [ε] (Example 4.3 (i)). A δ-valuation is an element of V(†D^⊚) mapping to an element of V^{±un} via this orbit. Equivalently, intrinsically in terms of the D-NF-bridge †φ^NF_*, a δ-valuation is a valuation lying in the image via †φ^NF_* of the unique †𝔇_j for which the bijection LabCusp(†D^⊚) ⥲ LabCusp(†𝔇_j) induced by †φ^NF_* maps δ to the element labeled 1.
explicit_hypotheses: †F^⊛, †F^⊚ as in Example 5.1 (iii)
δ ∈ LabCusp(†D^⊚)
IUT1.Ex5_4.iii.conclusion: Definition of δ-valuations, with the claim ("one verifies immediately") that the two descriptions agree.
obligations: Prove the equivalence of the two descriptions of δ-valuations; the text says it is verified immediately.

IUT1.Ex5_4.iv.content: Localizing at the δ-valuations gives an F-prime-strip †F^⊚|_δ, well defined up to isomorphism, from †F^⊚ (that is, from Õ^{⊛×} with its π1(†D^⊚)-action): at nonarchimedean δ-valuations via p-adic Frobenioids of the pairs Π_{p_0} ↷ Ô^▷_{p_0} restricted to open subgroups determined by δ (tempered analogues at bad v via [SemiAnbd] Theorem 6.6), at archimedean ones via [AbsTopIII] Corollaries 2.8, 2.9. A poly-morphism ‡𝔉 → †F^⊚ is a full poly-isomorphism ‡𝔉 ⥲ †F^⊚|_δ for some δ; it lies over a poly-morphism ‡𝔇 → †D^⊚, is fixed under pre-composition with Aut(‡𝔉) and post-composition with Aut_ε(†F^⊚), and is compatible with the local and global ∞κ-coric structures: restriction of Kummer classes gives poly-morphisms of pseudo-monoids {π1^rat(†D^⊛) ↷ †M^⊛_{∞κ} → ‡M_{∞κv} ⊆ ‡M_{∞κ×v}}_{v∈V}, equivariant for π1^rat(‡D_v) → π1^rat(†D^⊛). Poly-morphisms from a capsule {^e𝔉}_{e∈E} to †F^⊚ (respectively †𝔉) are collections of poly-morphisms.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_4.iii
‡𝔉 an F-prime-strip with associated D-prime-strip ‡𝔇
IUT1.Ex5_4.iv.conclusion: Construction of †F^⊚|_δ up to isomorphism and definition of poly-morphisms ‡𝔉 → †F^⊚, with the claims that they are invariant under the stated compositions and compatible with ∞κ-coric structures.
obligations: The localization at bad v uses the mono-anabelian algorithm implicit in the proof of [SemiAnbd] Theorem 6.6; at archimedean v [AbsTopIII] Corollaries 2.8, 2.9.
ambiguities: The global data in the domain of the Kummer display is defined only up to inner automorphisms of π1^rat(†D^⊛), the local data in the codomain only up to automorphisms of ‡𝔉 (page 149).

IUT1.Ex5_4.v.content: By Corollary 5.3 (ii) there is a unique poly-morphism †ψ^NF_* : †𝔉_J → †F^⊚ lying over †φ^NF_*.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_4.iv
IUT1.Ex5_4.v.conclusion: Existence and uniqueness of †ψ^NF_* lying over †φ^NF_*.
obligations: Derive from Corollary 5.3 (ii); the text gives the citation only, and the passage from isomorphisms of F-prime-strips to poly-morphisms into †F^⊚ is not spelled out.

IUT1.Ex5_4.vi.content: Since †F^⊛_mod is defined via terminal objects of †D^⊛, any poly-morphism †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} → †F^⊚ induces by restriction, for each v_{⟨J⟩} ∈ V_{⟨J⟩}, an isomorphism class of functors (†F^⊚ → †F^⊛ ⊇) †F^⊛_mod ⥲ †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} → †F_{v_{⟨J⟩}} independent of the choice of the poly-morphism among its F_l^*-conjugates. Collecting these gives isomorphism classes of restriction functors †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} → †𝔉_{⟨J⟩}, †F^⊛_J → †𝔉_J, †F^⊛_j → †𝔉_j, and their realifications †F^{⊛R}_{⟨J⟩} → †𝔉^R_{⟨J⟩}, †F^{⊛R}_J → †𝔉^R_J, †F^{⊛R}_j → †𝔉^R_j.
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_4.v
IUT1.Ex5_4.vi.conclusion: Construction of the restriction functor classes, with the claim that they are fixed by the indeterminacies in the choice of †𝔉_{⟨J⟩} → †F^⊚.
obligations: Prove that the isomorphism class of the restriction functor is independent of the F_l^*-conjugate chosen; the text attributes this to the definition of †F^⊛_mod via terminal objects and of F_mod in Definition 3.1 (b).
ambiguities: When v_{⟨J⟩} is archimedean, †F_{v_{⟨J⟩}} denotes by abuse of notation the category portion of the collection of data of Definition 5.2 (i) (b) (page 150).

IUT1.Ex5_4.vii.content: The objects of (vi) in the case j = 1, †F^⊛_pvt → †𝔉_pvt and †F^{⊛R}_pvt → †𝔉^R_pvt, are called pivotal distributions (Fig. 5.2).
explicit_hypotheses: the notation of IUT1.Ex5_4.vi
IUT1.Ex5_4.vii.conclusion: Definition of pivotal distributions as the case j = 1 of (vi).
ambiguities: J is identified with F_l^* elsewhere; "j = 1" presupposes such a labeling of J, which these pages do not restate.

IUT1.Rem5_4_2.content: Log-volumes (arithmetic degrees) on the copies of †F^⊛_mod. (i) Viewing †F^⊛_j as a section over †F^⊛_mod (like K over F_mod), log-volumes of †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} differ by a factor l* (the cardinality of J ⥲ F_l^*) from those of †F^⊛_j: arithmetic degrees on the factors of †F^⊛_J are averaged over J, analogous to normalized heights invariant under base change ([GenEll] Definition 1.2 (i)). (ii) Working with isomorphisms of Frobenioids such as †F^⊛_j ⥲ †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩}, arithmetic degree is intrinsic ([FrdI] Theorem 6.4 (iv)), so degrees on the factors are summed over J without dividing by l*, analogous to heights multiplied by the field degree.

IUT1.Rem5_4_2.conclusion: Two viewpoints on arithmetic degrees on †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} relative to †F^⊛_J: resulting averages (i) and resulting sums (ii), differing by the factor l*.
obligations: A formalization must fix which normalization (average or sum) is used wherever log-volumes on †F^⊛_{⟨J⟩} enter later estimates.
ambiguities: Both normalizations are offered as ways of thinking; the remark does not say which one a later computation uses.

IUT1.Def5_5.content: Notation: 𝔉 and 𝔇 denote F- and D-prime-strips. (i) An NF-bridge is (‡𝔉_J → ‡F^⊚ ⇢ ‡F^⊛) with arrow ‡ψ^NF_* where: (a) ‡𝔉_J = {‡𝔉_j}_{j∈J} is a capsule of F-prime-strips over a finite index set J with associated capsule ‡𝔇_J; (b) ‡F^⊚, ‡F^⊛ are categories equivalent to †F^⊚, †F^⊛ of Example 5.1 (iii), with natural Frobenioid structures and base categories ‡D^⊚, ‡D^⊛; (c) the dashed arrow is a morphism ‡D^⊚ → ‡D^⊛ abstractly equivalent to †D^⊚ → †D^⊛, with an isomorphism ‡F^⊚ ⥲ ‡F^⊛|_{‡D^⊚}; (d) ‡ψ^NF_* is a poly-morphism lifting (uniquely, Corollary 5.3 (ii)) a poly-morphism ‡φ^NF_* : ‡𝔇_J → ‡D^⊚ that forms a D-NF-bridge. Morphisms of NF-bridges: a capsule-full poly-isomorphism ¹𝔉_{J1} ⥲ ²𝔉_{J2}, a poly-isomorphism ¹F^⊚ ⥲ ²F^⊚ lifting a poly-isomorphism ¹D^⊚ ⥲ ²D^⊚ such that the induced pair forms a morphism of D-NF-bridges, and an isomorphism ¹F^⊛ ⥲ ²F^⊛, compatible with the ψ^NF and the dashed arrows. (ii) A Θ-bridge is (‡𝔉_J → ‡𝔉_> ⇢ ‡HT^Θ) with arrow ‡ψ^Θ_* where ‡𝔉_J is as before, ‡HT^Θ is a Θ-Hodge theater, ‡𝔉_> is the F-prime-strip tautologically associated to ‡HT^Θ (with D-prime-strip ‡𝔇_>), and ‡ψ^Θ_* = {‡ψ^Θ_j} is determined (Remark 5.3.1) by a D-Θ-bridge ‡φ^Θ_*. Morphisms: a capsule-full poly-isomorphism of capsules, the full poly-isomorphism ¹𝔉_> ⥲ ²𝔉_>, and an isomorphism of Θ-Hodge theaters (Remark 3.6.2), compatible with the ψ^Θ and dashed arrows. (iii) A ΘNF-Hodge theater is ‡HT^{ΘNF} = (‡F^⊛ ⇠ ‡F^⊚ ← ‡𝔉_J → ‡𝔉_> ⇢ ‡HT^Θ) in which the left part is an NF-bridge, the right part a Θ-bridge, and the associated data {‡φ^NF_*, ‡φ^Θ_*} form a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater; morphisms are pairs of morphisms of the NF- and Θ-bridges inducing the same bijection of the index sets of the capsules.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (Definition 3.1)
IUT1.Def5_5.conclusion: Definitions of NF-bridges, Θ-bridges, ΘNF-Hodge theaters and their [iso]morphisms. The text adds that one verifies immediately that each object determines an associated D-object (D-NF-bridge, D-Θ-bridge, D-ΘNF-Hodge theater) and that each morphism induces a morphism of the associated D-objects, with evident composition.
obligations: Definition. A formalization needs Frobenioids, F- and D-prime-strips and Θ-Hodge theaters, none of which is in Mathlib, and must check the "verifies immediately" claims about associated D-objects.
ambiguities: Morphisms of Θ-bridges use isomorphisms of Θ-Hodge theaters (Remark 3.6.2), whose definition is left to the reader there.
"Compatible in the evident sense" (pages 152 and 153) is not spelled out.

IUT1.Cor5_6.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) the natural functorially induced map from the set of isomorphisms between two Θ-Hodge theaters to the set of isomorphisms between the associated D-prime-strips is bijective; (ii) the natural map from isomorphisms between two NF-bridges (respectively Θ-bridges, ΘNF-Hodge theaters) to isomorphisms between the associated D-NF-bridges (respectively D-Θ-bridges, D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters) is bijective; (iii) given an NF-bridge and a Θ-bridge, the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms between their capsules of F-prime-strips that glue them into a ΘNF-Hodge theater is an F_l^*-torsor.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data (Definition 3.1)
two Θ-Hodge theaters (i); two NF-bridges, Θ-bridges or ΘNF-Hodge theaters (ii); an NF-bridge and a Θ-bridge (iii)
IUT1.Cor5_6.conclusion: (i), (ii): the stated maps on isomorphism sets are bijections. (iii): the gluing set is an F_l^*-torsor.

IUT1.Ex6_2.content: Model base-Θ^±-bridges. Notation: 𝔇 denotes a D-prime-strip. (i) Regard F_l as an F_l^±-group. (ii) The data (𝔇_±, 𝔇_≻, φ^{Θ±}_±) admit a natural poly-automorphism −1_{F_l} of order two: multiplication by −1 on F_l, with poly-isomorphisms 𝔇_t ⥲ 𝔇_{−t} and 𝔇_≻ ⥲ 𝔇_≻ given by the +-full poly-automorphism whose sign at every v is negative. (iii) For α ∈ {±1}^V, a natural poly-automorphism α^{Θ±} of order 1 or 2: the identity on F_l and the α-signed +-full poly-automorphism on each 𝔇_t and on 𝔇_≻.

IUT1.Ex6_3.content: Model base-Θ^ell-bridges. (i) Regard F_l as an F_l^±-torsor; take 𝔇_t, 𝔇_± as in Example 6.2 (i) and D^{⊚±} as in Definition 6.1 (v). Fix an isomorphism of F_l^±-torsors LabCusp^±(D^{⊚±}) ⥲ F_l; it induces an identification Aut_±(D^{⊚±})/Aut_csp(D^{⊚±}) ⥲ F_l^{⋊±}. At v ∈ V^good ∩ V^non (respectively V^bad) restriction along X_{→v} → X_v → X_K (respectively X_v with double underline → X_v → X_K), the coverings of Definition 3.1 (e), (f), gives a natural morphism φ^{Θell}_{•,v} : D_v → D^{⊚±}; at archimedean v a tautological morphism D_v = X_v → X_v ⥲ X(D^{⊚±}, v) gives the same. For each v, φ^{Θell}_{v_0} : D_{v_0} → D^{⊚±} is the poly-morphism of all β ∘ φ^{Θell}_{•,v} ∘ α with α ∈ Aut_+(D_{v_0}), β ∈ Aut_csp(D^{⊚±}); these give φ^{Θell}_0 : 𝔇_0 → D^{⊚±}; post-composing with the poly-action of t ∈ F_l ⊆ F_l^{⋊±} gives φ^{Θell}_t : 𝔇_t → D^{⊚±}, and φ^{Θell}_± : 𝔇_± → D^{⊚±} is the collection. IUT1.Def6_4.content: Put l^± = l* + 1 = (l+1)/2. (i) A D-Θ^±-bridge is a poly-morphism †φ^{Θ±}_± : †𝔇_T → †𝔇_≻ with †𝔇_≻ a D-prime-strip, T an F_l^±-group and †𝔇_T = {†𝔇_t}_{t∈T} a capsule of D-prime-strips, such that there are isomorphisms 𝔇_≻ ⥲ †𝔇_≻ and 𝔇_± ⥲ †𝔇_T whose induced bijection F_l ⥲ T is an isomorphism of F_l^±-groups and conjugation by which maps φ^{Θ±}_± ↦ †φ^{Θ±}_±. †𝔇_{|T|} is the l^±-capsule obtained by passing to |T| = T/{±1} and identifying the components in each fiber via the constituents of †φ^{Θ±}_± (each constituent well defined only up to a positive automorphism), and †𝔇_{T*} is the l*-capsule for T* = |T| \ {0}. A morphism is a pair: a capsule-+-full poly-isomorphism †𝔇_T ⥲ ‡𝔇_{T'} inducing an isomorphism of F_l^±-groups T ⥲ T', and a +-full poly-isomorphism †𝔇_≻ ⥲ ‡𝔇_≻, compatible with the bridges. (ii) A D-Θ^ell-bridge is a poly-morphism †φ^{Θell}_± : †𝔇_T → †D^{⊚±} with †D^{⊚±} equivalent to D^{⊚±}, T an F_l^±-torsor, such that isomorphisms D^{⊚±} ⥲ †D^{⊚±} and 𝔇_± ⥲ †𝔇_T exist inducing an isomorphism of F_l^±-torsors and mapping φ^{Θell}_± ↦ †φ^{Θell}_±. Morphisms: a capsule-+-full poly-isomorphism inducing an isomorphism of F_l^±-torsors, and an Aut_csp-orbit of isomorphisms †D^{⊚±} → ‡D^{⊚±}, compatible with the bridges. (iii) A D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater is †HT^{D-Θ±ell} = (†𝔇_≻ ← †𝔇_T → †D^{⊚±}) with T an F_l^±-group, a D-Θ^±-bridge and a D-Θ^ell-bridge (for the induced torsor structure), such that isomorphisms to the models exist mapping φ^{Θ±}_± ↦ †φ^{Θ±}_± and φ^{Θell}_± ↦ †φ^{Θell}_± simultaneously; a morphism is a pair of morphisms of the two bridges inducing the same poly-isomorphism of capsules.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data

IUT1.Prop6_5.content: Let †HT^{D-Θ±ell} = (†𝔇_≻ ← †𝔇_T → †D^{⊚±}) be a D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater. (i) For v ∈ V, t ∈ T, the D-Θ^ell-bridge induces a single, well defined bijection †ζ^{Θell}_{v_t} : LabCusp^±(†D_{v_t}) ⥲ LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}) compatible with the F_l^±-torsor structures; for w ∈ V the bijection †ξ^{Θell}_{v_t,w_t} = (†ζ^{Θell}_{w_t})^{-1} ∘ †ζ^{Θell}_{v_t} is compatible with the F_l^±-group structures; identifying via these gives an F_l^±-group LabCusp^±(†𝔇_t) and a well defined bijection †ζ^{Θell}_t : LabCusp^±(†𝔇_t) ⥲ LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}) compatible with the torsor structures. (ii) The D-Θ^±-bridge induces well defined bijections †ζ^{Θ±}_{v_t} : LabCusp^±(†D_{v_t}) ⥲ LabCusp^±(†D_{≻,v}) compatible with the F_l^±-group structures; the bijections †ξ^{Θ±}_{≻,v,w} = (†ζ^{Θ±}_{w_0}) ∘ †ξ^{Θell}_{v_0,w_0} ∘ (†ζ^{Θ±}_{v_0})^{-1} and †ξ^{Θ±}_{v_t,w_t} = (†ζ^{Θ±}_{w_t})^{-1} ∘ †ξ^{Θ±}_{≻,v,w} ∘ †ζ^{Θ±}_{v_t} are compatible with the group structures, with †ξ^{Θ±}_{v_t,w_t} = †ξ^{Θell}_{v_t,w_t}; this gives an F_l^±-group LabCusp^±(†𝔇_≻) and well defined bijections †ζ^{Θ±}_t : LabCusp^±(†𝔇_t) ⥲ LabCusp^±(†𝔇_≻) compatible with the group structures. (iii) T ∋ t ↦ †ζ^{Θell}_t(0) defines a well defined bijection (†ζ_±)^{-1} : T ⥲ LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}) compatible with the torsor structures, and for t ∈ T the composite (†ζ^{Θell}_0)^{-1} ∘ †ζ^{Θell}_t ∘ (†ζ^{Θ±}_t)^{-1} ∘ †ζ^{Θ±}_0 of LabCusp^±(†𝔇_0) is the action, for its F_l^±-group structure, of (†ζ^{Θell}_0)^{-1}((†ζ_±)^{-1}(t)). (iv) For α ∈ Aut_±(†D^{⊚±})/Aut_csp(†D^{⊚±}), replacing †φ^{Θell}_± by α ∘ †φ^{Θell}_± changes each †ζ^{Θell}_t by post-composition with the image of α under the natural bijection Aut_±/Aut_csp ⥲ Aut_±(LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±})) (≅ F_l^{⋊±}).

IUT1.Prop6_6.content: (i) Isomorphisms of D-Θ^±-bridges form a torsor over {±1} × ∏_{v∈V}{±1}. (ii) Isomorphisms of D-Θ^ell-bridges form an F_l^{⋊±}-torsor. (iii) Isomorphisms of D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theaters form a {±1}-torsor. (iv) Gluings form a torsor over F_l^{⋊±} × ∏_{v∈V}{±1}. (v) A functorial algorithm constructs a D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater from a D-Θ^ell-bridge, up to the indeterminacy of (iv).

IUT1.Prop6_7.content: Let †φ^{Θ±}_± : †𝔇_T → †𝔇_≻ be a D-Θ^±-bridge. Replacing †𝔇_T by †𝔇_{T*}, identifying †𝔇_≻ with †𝔇_0 via †φ^{Θ±}_0 to form a D-prime-strip †𝔇_>, replacing the +-full poly-morphisms in †φ^{Θ±}_± at v ∈ V^good by the corresponding full poly-morphisms and those at v ∈ V^bad by the poly-morphisms of Example 4.4 (i), (ii) (described via group-theoretic algorithms), gives a functorial algorithm constructing a D-Θ-bridge †φ^Θ_* : †𝔇_{T*} → †𝔇_> as in Definition 4.6 (ii), well defined up to a unique isomorphism. The correspondences †𝔇_T|_{T \ {0}} ↦ †𝔇_{T*} and †𝔇_0, †𝔇_≻ ↦ †𝔇_> each map precisely two D-prime-strips to one.

IUT1.Prop6_8.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) Associating to a D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater its underlying D-Θ^ell-bridge is a natural functor (isomorphisms to isomorphisms) whose output admits an F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry, a symmetry by a finite group with a natural outer isomorphism to F_l^{⋊±}, acting doubly transitively (transitively with stabilizers of order two) on the index set T. (ii) Associating the l^±-capsule †𝔇_{|T|} of the underlying D-Θ^±-bridge is a natural functor to l^±-capsules of D-prime-strips with capsule-full poly-isomorphisms, whose output admits an S_{l^±}-symmetry acting transitively on |T|; it forgets the labels in |F_l| = F_l/{±1}, so that, given only †𝔇_{|T|} up to isomorphism, there are precisely l^± possibilities for the element of |F_l| corresponding to a given index. (iii) Composing (ii) with mono-analyticization (Definition 4.1 (iv)) gives a natural functor to l^±-capsules of D^⊢-prime-strips with the same symmetry properties.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
IUT1.Prop6_8.conclusion: Three natural functors from the category of D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theaters (with isomorphisms), with output symmetries F_l^{⋊±} (doubly transitive on T), S_{l^±} (transitive on |T|), and the same for the mono-analytic capsules.
obligations: Proof (page 168): assertions (i), (ii), (iii) "follow immediately from the definitions", with Proposition 6.6 (ii) for (i).
The double transitivity in (i) is an elementary fact about F_l^{⋊±} = F_l ⋊ {±1} acting on F_l by z ↦ ±z + λ and could be checked independently.

IUT1.Prop6_9.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data: (i) Given a D-Θ^±-bridge †φ^{Θ±}_± : †𝔇_T → †𝔇_≻, let Prc(†𝔇_T) be the l^±-procession of D-prime-strips formed by the subcapsules of †𝔇_{|T|} corresponding to S^±_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ S^±_t = {0, 1, ..., t−1} ⊆ ... ⊆ S^±_{l^±} = |F_l| (Fig. 6.2), via |T| ⥲ |F_l|. Then †φ^{Θ±}_± ↦ Prc(†𝔇_T) is a natural functor to processions of D-prime-strips, whose output has, for each n ∈ {1, ..., l^±}, precisely n possibilities for the element of |F_l| corresponding to a given index of the n-capsule; hence, pre-composed with †HT^{D-Θ±ell} ↦ †φ^{Θ±}_±, the indeterminacy of (l^±)^{(l^±)} possibilities of Proposition 6.8 (ii) is reduced to l^±! possibilities. (ii) Composing with mono-analyticization gives a functor φ ↦ Prc(†𝔇^⊢_T) with the same indeterminacy properties. (iii) These functors are compatible with those of Proposition 4.11 (i), (ii) via Proposition 6.7: the inclusions S*_j = {1, ..., j} ↪ S^±_t = {0, 1, ..., t−1}, for j ∈ {1, ..., l*} and t = j + 1, determine natural transformations Prc(†𝔇_{T*}) ↪ Prc(†𝔇_T) and Prc(†𝔇^⊢_{T*}) ↪ Prc(†𝔇^⊢_T).

a D-Θ^±-bridge †φ^{Θ±}_± : †𝔇_T → †𝔇_≻ (Definition 6.4 (i))
IUT1.Prop6_9.conclusion: Natural functors to processions with indeterminacy n at the n-th capsule, total indeterminacy l^±! instead of (l^±)^{(l^±)}, and natural transformations relating them to the functors of Proposition 4.11 through Proposition 6.7.
obligations: Proof (page 170): assertions (i), (ii), (iii) "follow immediately from the definitions".
The counting claim ∏_{n=1}^{l^±} n = l^±! versus (l^±)^{(l^±)} is elementary and could be checked in Lean independently of the rest.
ambiguities: In (i), nonnegative integers stand by abuse of notation for their images in |F_l| (page 169).

IUT1.Cor6_10.content: The D-Θ^{±ell}-link between D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theaters is the full poly-isomorphism of the mono-analytic D^⊢-prime-strips D^⊢_>; the resulting étale-picture with its symmetries.

IUT1.Def6_11.content: (i) Θ^±-bridge: a poly-morphism F_T → F_≻ of F-prime-strips lifting a D-Θ^±-bridge (Corollary 5.3 (ii)); capsules F_{|T|}, F_{T^*}. (ii) Θ^ell-bridge: F_T → D^{⊚±}, which is by definition a D-Θ^ell-bridge on the associated capsule of D-prime-strips. (iii) Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater: a Θ^±-bridge and a Θ^ell-bridge whose associated D-data form a D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater; morphisms induce the same poly-isomorphism of capsules.

IUT1.Cor6_12.content: (i) Isomorphisms of Θ^±-bridges, Θ^ell-bridges, Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theaters biject with those of the associated D-objects. (ii) Gluings of a Θ^±-bridge and a Θ^ell-bridge form a torsor over F_l^{⋊±} × ∏_{v∈V}{±1}.

IUT1.Rem6_12_2.content: Relative to fixed initial Θ-data. (i) Let (†𝔉_T → †𝔉_≻) be a Θ^±-bridge with associated D-Θ^±-bridge (†𝔇_T → †𝔇_≻) (Definition 6.11 (i)); Proposition 6.7 gives a D-Θ-bridge (†𝔇_{T*} → †𝔇_>). If this arises from a Θ-bridge (‡𝔉_J → ‡𝔉_> ⇢ ‡HT^Θ) (so J = T*), then the portion ‡𝔉_J → ‡𝔉_>, being completely determined by its D-Θ-bridge (Definition 5.5 (ii) (d)), may be regarded as constructed from the Θ^±-bridge by a functorial algorithm similar to that of Proposition 6.7; and since isomorphisms of Θ-bridges correspond bijectively to those of the associated D-Θ-bridges (Corollary 5.6 (ii)), they correspond bijectively to isomorphisms of these portions (Corollary 5.3 (ii)). The Θ-bridge is then said to be glued to the Θ^±-bridge via the functorial algorithm of Proposition 6.7; explicit descriptions are left to the reader, with a similar construction for D-Θ- and D-Θ^±-bridges. (ii) Gluing a Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater (Definition 6.11 (iii)) to a ΘNF-Hodge theater (Definition 5.5 (iii)) along the associated Θ^±- and Θ-bridges via Proposition 6.7 gives a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater (Definition 6.13 (i)); by Proposition 4.8 (ii) and Corollary 5.6 (ii) the gluing isomorphism is unique, and analogues of Propositions 4.8, 6.6 and Corollaries 5.6, 6.12 may be verified; similarly a D-Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater and a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater glue to a D-Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater (Definition 6.13 (ii)); routine details are left to the reader.
explicit_hypotheses: a fixed collection of initial Θ-data
(i): a Θ^±-bridge and a Θ-bridge whose D-Θ-bridge is obtained from the associated D-Θ^±-bridge by Proposition 6.7
IUT1.Rem6_12_2.conclusion: Definition of gluing a Θ-bridge to a Θ^±-bridge via Proposition 6.7; uniqueness of the gluing isomorphism between a Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater and a ΘNF-Hodge theater; the analogues of Propositions 4.8, 6.6 and Corollaries 5.6, 6.12 for Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theaters.
obligations: The functorial algorithm of (i) and the analogues in (ii) are not written out; "the routine details" are left to the reader twice (pages 174, 175).
Uniqueness of the gluing isomorphism is derived from Proposition 4.8 (ii) and Corollary 5.6 (ii).

IUT1.Rem6_12_3.content: (i) A ΘNF-Hodge theater may be thought of as a total space of a local system of F_l^*-torsors, and a Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater of F_l^{⋊±}-torsors, over a base space representing a homotopy between a number field and a Tate curve. These torsors arise from l-torsion points (discrete approximations of the elliptic curve over a number field, [HASurI] §1.3.4) and, via tempered fundamental groups at bad v, as finite approximations of the copy of Z that is the Galois group of a tempered covering of the Tate curve ([EtTh] Remark 2.16.2); in a Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater the additive and multiplicative structures of this Z occur independently, extracted from the entanglement in a ring. (ii) The local-system copy of Z recalls the Teichmüller-theoretic viewpoint of [AbsTopIII] §I5, corresponding in p-adic Teichmüller theory to a nilpotent ordinary indigenous bundle. (iii) The two combinatorial dimensions (additive F_l^{⋊±}, multiplicative F_l^*) correspond to two real dimensions of transformations of the upper half-plane: z ↦ z + a, z ↦ −z̄ + a, and z ↦ (z·cos t − sin t)/(z·sin t + cos t), z ↦ (z̄·cos t + sin t)/(z̄·sin t − cos t) (a, t ∈ R). The additive symmetry relates to q = e^{2πiz} and fixes the cusp at infinity (combinatorial prototype: cusp); the multiplicative symmetry relates to w = (z − i)/(z + i) and acts transitively on the boundary (prototype: node of a mod p Hecke correspondence). The only coric symmetries, common to both, are {±1} (z ↦ z, −z̄). Fig. 6.4 tabulates the comparison.
IUT1.Rem6_12_3.conclusion: Heuristic analogy. The concrete content is the list of transformations of the upper half-plane on page 176: the additive family z ↦ z + a, z ↦ −z̄ + a, said to fix the cusp at infinity and to relate to q = e^{2πiz}; the multiplicative family, said to act transitively on the boundary and to relate to w = (z − i)/(z + i); and the statement (page 177) that the symmetries common to both are z ↦ z, −z̄, compared with {±1}. Fig. 6.4 on page 178 tabulates the comparison.
obligations: The statements about the two families of transformations on pages 176 and 177 are elementary and could be checked in Lean independently.
ambiguities: Whether the multiplicative family with t ∈ R and the additive family with a ∈ R meet exactly in z ↦ z and z ↦ −z̄ depends on the parametrization; the page states this without computation.

IUT1.Rem6_12_4.content: (i) Like the F_l^*-symmetry of Proposition 4.9 (i), the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of Proposition 6.8 (i) will be used ([IUTchII], [IUTchIII]) to build an explicit network of comparison isomorphisms relating objects such as log-volumes on the non-labeled prime-strips it permutes, without label crushing (preserving the bijection between indices and labels in T ⥲ F_l); this synchronization of labels is essentially a consequence of the single connected component (single basepoint) of the global object †D^{⊚±} (respectively †D^⊚). (ii) Concretely, it is realized by the bijections †ζ_* : LabCusp(†D^⊚) ⥲ J and †ζ_± : LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}) ⥲ T of Propositions 4.7 (iii), 6.5 (iii); these bijections between index sets of capsules and sets of global (±-)label classes of cusps distinguish the combinatorially holomorphic F_l^*- and F_l^{⋊±}-symmetries (Propositions 4.9 (i), 6.8 (i)) from the combinatorially real analytic S_{l*}- and S_{l^±}-symmetries (Propositions 4.9 (ii), (iii); 6.8 (ii), (iii)). (iii) The additive theory has global ±-synchronization: the isomorphisms †ξ of Proposition 6.5 (i), (ii) between the ±-indeterminacies at the various v. This is a necessary precondition for the additive portion F_l ⊆ F_l^{⋊±} of the symmetry, since the additive action of F_l on itself is not compatible with F_l ↠ |F_l|. (iv) Both the †ζ's and the †ξ's are constructed by functorial algorithms from the intrinsic structure of the Hodge theater, not by comparison with a fixed reference model such as the objects of Examples 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 6.2, 6.3; this matters when combining with the log-shells of [AbsTopIII] in [IUTchIII].
IUT1.Rem6_12_4.conclusion: Interpretive summary; the mathematical claims cited are Propositions 4.7 (iii), 6.5, 4.9, 6.8, plus the elementary observation that translation by F_l does not descend to |F_l| = F_l/{±1}.
obligations: The observation in (iii) that the additive action of F_l on F_l is not compatible with F_l ↠ F_l/{±1} (for l odd) is elementary and could be checked in Lean.

"Constructed by functorial algorithms from the intrinsic structure" (iv) is a property a formalization would need to make precise (for instance, as naturality with respect to isomorphisms of Hodge theaters).
ambiguities: Page 177 writes †ζ_± : LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}) ⥲ T, whereas Proposition 6.5 (iii) constructs (†ζ_±)^{-1} : T ⥲ LabCusp^±(†D^{⊚±}); the two agree.

IUT1.Rem6_12_5.content: (i) A fundamental difference between the F_l^*-symmetry of §4 and the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of §6 is the inclusion of the zero element of F_l, which lets the network of comparison isomorphisms relate the zero-labeled prime-strip to the nonzero-labeled ones, in a combinatorially holomorphic fashion compatible with the bijections †ζ; evaluation at torsion points related to the zero-labeled cusps (Example 4.4 (i)) is important for the normalization of the étale theta function ([EtTh] Theorem 1.10, functions of standard type; [IUTchII]). (ii) The disadvantage is that it does not insulate the nonzero-labeled prime-strips from confusion with the zero-labeled one; this matters for the Gaussian Frobenioids of [IUTchII], arising from the theta values {q_v^{j²}}_j (q double-underlined, j underlined) at the non-zero-labeled evaluation points (Example 4.4), which are later related to global arithmetic line bundles on F using both additive and multiplicative structures, hence §5. (iii) Since no analogues of Gaussian Frobenioids involving the zero-labeled points will be needed, no additive analogue of the global Frobenioids of Example 5.1 is required.
IUT1.Rem6_12_5.conclusion: Methodological remark: the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry relates zero- and nonzero-labeled prime-strips but cannot separate them; no additive analogue of Example 5.1 is needed.
ambiguities: "Confusion" of zero- and nonzero-labeled prime-strips (page 180) is informal.

IUT1.Rem6_12_6.content: (i) Another difference: the single basepoint underlying the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry is geometric. The labels in T ⥲ F_l of a (D-)Θ^{±ell}-Hodge theater correspond throughout to collections of cusps in a single copy (connected component) of D_v at each v, permuted by the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry of the (D-)Θ^ell-bridge (Proposition 6.8 (i)) without permuting the valuations V^± ⊆ V(K) (Definition 6.1 (v)); by contrast the single basepoint of the F_l^*-symmetry of §4 is arithmetic: F_l^* (Proposition 4.9 (i)) permutes the F_l^*-translates of V^± = V^{±un} ⊆ V^Bor ⊆ V(K) (Example 4.3 (i), Remark 6.1.1). (ii) The geometric basepoint suits the Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation of the étale theta function ([IUTchII]), where a single connected component of D_v at bad v is central. (iii) The arithmetic basepoint suits the explicit construction of F_mod (Example 5.1), an object invariant under the F_l^*-symmetries Aut(C_K)/Aut_ε(C_K) ⥲ F_l^* of Example 4.3 (iv); carrying out Example 5.1 with D^{⊚±} would sacrifice the F_l^*-rigidity with respect to Aut(D^{⊚±})/Aut_±(D^{⊚±}) ⥲ F_l^* (Definition 6.1 (v); Example 6.3; Definition 6.4 (ii)), losing the single geometric basepoint and compatibility with [IUTchII]. (iv) This reflects that the Borel subgroup {(∗ ∗; 0 ∗)} ⊆ SL_2(F_l) is normally terminal (Example 4.3), whereas the semi-unipotent subgroup {(±1 ∗; 0 ±1)} ⊆ SL_2(F_l), corresponding to Aut_±(D^{⊚±}) ⊆ Aut(D^{⊚±}), is not. (v) A (D-)Θ^{±ell}NF-Hodge theater is an intricate relay between geometric and arithmetic basepoints allowing both (a) the evaluation theory of [IUTchII] and (b) the construction of F_mod in Example 5.1; with F_l viewed as a finite approximation of Z, this is a global combinatorial resolution of the additive and multiplicative dimensions of Z ([AbsTopIII] Remark 5.6.1). Computationally it is natural to regard F_l as a good approximation of Z when l is sufficiently large, as in [GenEll] §4 (Remark 3.1.2 (iv)).
IUT1.Rem6_12_6.conclusion: Interpretive remark. Mathematical content: (a) the F_l^{⋊±}-symmetry permutes cusps without permuting V^±, while the F_l^*-symmetry permutes F_l^*-translates of V^±; (b) the Borel subgroup of SL_2(F_l) is normally terminal, the semi-unipotent subgroup is not.
obligations: Claim (iv) on normal terminality in SL_2(F_l) is elementary finite group theory and could be checked in Lean (for the semi-unipotent subgroup, its normalizer contains the diagonal torus, so it is not normally terminal; for the Borel subgroup, it is self-normalizing); the text gives no proof on these pages, referring to Example 4.3 for the Borel case.
The correspondence of the semi-unipotent subgroup with Aut_±(D^{⊚±}) ⊆ Aut(D^{⊚±}) is asserted with reference to Definition 6.1 (v).
ambiguities: In the display of the semi-unipotent subgroup (page 181) the two diagonal entries are written ±1 independently; inside SL_2(F_l) the determinant condition forces them to be equal, so the subgroup is {±1} times the unipotent radical.
"Normally terminal" means equal to its normalizer; the term is used without definition on these pages.

IUT1.Sec0.PseudoMonoid.content: A topological pseudo-monoid is a topological space P with a continuous map S → P, S ⊆ P × P, such that there are a topological abelian group M (written multiplicatively) and an embedding ι : P ↪ M with S = {(a, b) | ι(a)·ι(b) ∈ ι(P)} and S → P the restriction of the group law. With M discrete, P is a pseudo-monoid. P is divisible if M, ι can be chosen so that every element of M has n-th roots for all n ≥ 1 and a ∈ ι(P) if and only if a^n ∈ ι(P); P is cyclotomic if M, ι can be chosen with μ_M ≅ Q/Z, μ_M ⊆ ι(P) and μ_M·ι(P) ⊆ ι(P).

IUT1.Sec0.CapsuleMorphism.content: A morphism of capsules {A_j}_{j∈J} → {A'_{j'}}_{j'∈J'} consists of an injection ι : J ↪ J' and, for each j ∈ J, a morphism A_j → A'_{ι(j)}; capsules of objects of C form a category Capsule(C).
obligations: IUT.PaperI.Capsule.Hom, Hom.id and Hom.comp state the morphisms, identities and composition, but the category laws of Capsule(C) are not proved in Lean, so this record is not linked to a Lean declaration.

IUT1.Sec0.CapsuleFullPolyMorphism.content: A capsule-full poly-morphism {A_j}_{j∈J} → {A'_{j'}}_{j'∈J'} is the poly-morphism associated to a fixed injection ι : J ↪ J' consisting of the capsule morphisms given by collections of arbitrary isomorphisms A_j ⥲ A'_{ι(j)}, j ∈ J.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.

IUT1.Sec0.CapsuleFullPolyIsomorphism.content: A capsule-full poly-isomorphism is a capsule-full poly-morphism whose associated injection between index sets is a bijection.
obligations: IUT.PaperI.Capsule.IsCapsuleFullPolyIso states only the bijectivity condition on the injection ι, not the whole definition, so the record is not linked.

IUT1.Sec0.FiniteEtaleCategory.content: For a connected noetherian algebraic stack X that is generically scheme-like, B(X) is the category of finite étale coverings of X (with morphisms over X); for a noetherian ring A, B(A) = B(Spec(A)); B(X)^0 ⊆ B(X) is the subcategory of connected objects.
obligations: Algebraic stacks are not in Mathlib.

IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.content: For a topological group Π, B^temp(Π) is the category of countable discrete sets with continuous Π-action and Π-equivariant maps. Π is tempered if it is an inverse limit of an inverse system of surjections of countable discrete topological groups. A category equivalent to B^temp(Π) with Π tempered is a connected temperoid; then C ≃ (C^0)^⊤. For Galois-countable Π, Π is reconstructed up to inner automorphism from B^temp(Π) or B^temp(Π)^0, which defines π_1(C), π_1(C^0) for a Galois-countable connected temperoid C.
obligations: Tempered groups and temperoids are not in Mathlib; the reconstruction of π_1 cites Remark 2.5.3 (i), (T1), (T5). Tempered groups, B^temp(Π) and connected temperoids are defined in the fragments listed in `fragments`; the reconstruction of Π and of π_1, the subcategory of connected objects, and (C^0)^T are not formalized.

IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.tempered_gr.content: Definition: a group P with a topology is tempered if there exist a nonempty directed preorder I (in the universe of P), countable groups G i with the discrete topology, surjective homomorphisms G j -> G i for i <= j satisfying the identity and composition laws, and an isomorphism of topological groups from P onto the subgroup of compatible families of the product of the G i with the subspace topology of the product topology. Lemmas: invariance under isomorphism of topological groups; a countable discrete group is tempered; a group isomorphic to the limit of a surjective system of finite discrete groups is tempered; a tempered group is totally disconnected; the circle group is not tempered.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.tempered_gr.conclusion: A proposition (definition) with elementary lemmas, all proved.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.tempered_gr.covers: Page 34, the sentence defining a tempered topological group.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.tempered_gr.not_covered: B^temp(Pi), connected temperoids, the equivalence C = (C^0)^T, Galois-countability and the reconstruction of Pi and of pi_1(C), pi_1(C^0); that Z_p or any specific infinite profinite group is tempered.
ambiguities: The page states no condition on the index set of the inverse system; read as an arbitrary nonempty directed preorder, with no countability condition, in the universe of the group. [SemiAnbd] Definition 3.1 (i) was not read.

IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.btemp_categ.content: Definition: B^temp(P) is the full subcategory of Mathlib's category Action (Type u) P of P-sets and equivariant maps on the objects whose underlying set is countable and whose action map P x X -> X is continuous for the discrete topology on X. Lemma: a countable set with the trivial action is an object.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.btemp_categ.not_covered: The subcategory B^temp(Pi)^0 of connected objects (connected objects are defined in [FrdI], section 0, not read).

IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.connected_t.content: Definition: a category C is a connected temperoid if there is a topological group P (in a fixed universe u) that is tempered with C equivalent to B^temp(P). Lemma: B^temp(P) is a connected temperoid when P is a tempered topological group.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.connected_t.conclusion: A proposition (definition) with one proved lemma.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.connected_t.covers: Page 34, the sentence defining a connected temperoid.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.frag.connected_t.not_covered: C^0, (C^0)^T and the equivalence C = (C^0)^T; the reconstruction of Pi up to inner automorphism and pi_1(C), pi_1(C^0) for Galois-countable C.
ambiguities: The universe of the tempered group is a parameter of the definition.

IUT1.Sec0.TemperoidMorphism.content: For connected temperoids C_1, C_2, a morphism C_1 → C_2 is an isomorphism class of functors C_2 → C_1 preserving finite limits and countable colimits; a morphism C_1^0 → C_2^0 is a morphism (C_1^0)^⊤ → (C_2^0)^⊤. For Galois-countable tempered Π_1, Π_2 there are natural bijections between continuous outer homomorphisms Π_1 → Π_2, morphisms B^temp(Π_1) → B^temp(Π_2), and morphisms B^temp(Π_1)^0 → B^temp(Π_2)^0.
obligations: Temperoids are not in Mathlib. The isomorphism classes of exact countable functors that define a morphism are formalized in IUT1.Sec0.TemperoidMorphism.frag.morphism_class; morphisms C1^0 -> C2^0 and the bijections with outer homomorphisms are not.
ambiguities: Page 35 notes this differs slightly from [SemiAnbd] Definition 3.1 (iii).

IUT1.Sec0.TemperoidMorphism.frag.morphis.content: Definition: for categories C1, C2 (same object and morphism universes), the type of isomorphism classes (quotient by existence of a natural isomorphism) of functors C2 -> C1 that preserve finite limits and preserve colimits of every shape J : Type that is a countable category.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperoidMorphism.frag.morphis.covers: Page 35, the definition of a morphism C1 -> C2 of connected temperoids.
IUT1.Sec0.TemperoidMorphism.frag.morphis.not_covered: Morphisms C1^0 -> C2^0 (need (C^0)^T from [FrdI]); the natural bijections with continuous outer homomorphisms for Galois-countable tempered groups; the remark on abstract equivalence.
ambiguities: 'Preserves countable colimits' read as preserving colimits of every countable shape in Type, as Mathlib's PreservesFiniteLimits does for finite shapes; the page notes a slight difference from [SemiAnbd] Definition 3.1 (iii), which was not read.

IUT1.Sec0.AbstractlyEquivalent.content: Isomorphism classes of functors φ : C_1 → C_2 and φ' : C'_1 → C'_2 are abstractly equivalent if there are isomorphisms α_i : C_i ⥲ C'_i (i = 1, 2) with φ' ∘ α_1 = α_2 ∘ φ; the same terminology applies to morphisms of (connected) temperoids and of their subcategories of connected objects.

IUT1.Sec0.Valuations.content: NF, MLF, CAF abbreviate number field, mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field, complex archimedean field; Primes is the set of prime numbers. For a number field F, V(F) = V(F)^arc ∪ V(F)^non is the set of valuations (places) of F; F_v is the completion at v; an element is integral at v if of norm ≤ 1; for a Galois extension L of F, L_v is the completion at a valuation of L over v; p_v is the residue characteristic for nonarchimedean v and, for archimedean v, the positive real element of F_v with natural logarithm 1 (p_v = e). These notations extend to infinite extensions of Q by projective or inductive limits.
